articles.title: Lanterns Star Aaron Pierre Addresses DCU Future After James Gunn's Firing, "I'm Very At Peace"
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of HBO Aaron Pierre found out at the same time as everyone else that Skydance had fired James Gunn and Peter Safran from their positions leading the DC Universe (DCU). The man who played John Stewart in Lanterns was actually doing an interview the day it happened, and he had just learned the news before going on […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Aaron Pierre found out at the same time as everyone else that Skydance had fired James Gunn and Peter Safran from their positions leading the DC Universe (DCU). The man who played John Stewart in Lanterns was actually doing an interview the day it happened, and he had just learned the news before going on to talk to the interviewer. That made his comments at the time honest and open, as he hadn't had a chance to learn what his future in the DCU looked like, if it existed anymore at all. While he is appearing in Man of Tomorrow next year, what happens next remains a mystery.

In a podcast interview with IndieWire that was recorded the day that Gunn and Safran were fired, Pierre opened up about his feelings. "Well, I actually only just found out the news prior to logging on, so I haven’t very much time at all to process the enormity of that news," Pierre said. "But what I can say is that my relationship with James and my relationship with Peter is a beautiful relationship, and I’ve really loved every moment collaborating with them and working with them and getting to know them. And I’m excited to, beyond this point, in a different context, collaborate with them again, and I’m also excited to see what happens next for DC."

What Could Happen With Aaron Pierre's John Stewart in the DCU? Image Courtesy of HBO Max There is a lot of uncertainty surrounding the DCU right now. While it is true that Jeremy Latcham has replaced Gunn and Safran as the new head of the DCU, and he will answer directly to the studio heads, the way the franchise will go is unclear. There could be a brand-new fresh reboot, with Latcham starting over, but that risks losing a lot of fans who are tired of investing in a franchise that keeps rebooting. The movies could also play off what Gunn has already built, but with more of an emphasis on A-list heroes to try to bring in more money at the box office.

There are already rumors that Skydance wants to keep David Corenswet as Superman, although those same rumors indicate that the studio might want to recast some of the characters around him. There were also rumors that Skydance wanted to keep Robert Pattinson as Batman and maybe bring him into the main DCU, but with Pattinson signing on to be the next James Bond for Amazon MGM Studios, that is not likely to happen. While Pattinson could do it, carrying two major franchises as Batman and James Bond would likely be too much for the actor.

As for Green Lantern, there were also rumors that Skydance might want Hal Jordan back, which could be difficult because of what happened in Lanterns . James Gunn clearly set up John Stewart as the Green Lantern of his movie and TV world, but if Skydance wants Jordan, there isn't much room for Stewart without bringing in the Green Lantern Corps, something that is not as likely with Skydance wanting just A-list characters to ensure maximum profit potential. Instead, it seems that the studio wants a Justice League, and whether that includes John Stewart or Hal Jordan will determine Aaron Pierre's place in the franchise.

Do you want to see Aaron Pierre back as John Stewart in the DCU? Let us know what you want to see from the Green Lanterns in the future of movies and TV in the comments below.

articles.title: The DCU’s New Leader Made Two Non-Marvel Movies That Are Actually Masterpieces
articles.summary: For the past couple of weeks, everyone has been talking about DC Studios due to the news of James Gunn and Peter Safran's departure a mere year into their reported ten-year plan. For the most part, reception to the Gunn and Safran era of the franchise was positive and felt like a step in the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google For the past couple of weeks, everyone has been talking about DC Studios due to the news of James Gunn and Peter Safran's departure a mere year into their reported ten-year plan. For the most part, reception to the Gunn and Safran era of the franchise was positive and felt like a step in the right direction, so this came as a shock to many. It doesn't help that DC has gone through several major reboots, so another change at the helm feels like too many for fans, who might be willing to give up on their hope for a successful DC franchise.

However, Jeremy Latcham is now in as the new head of DC Studios and he has a pretty strong track record. Latcham has a history with Marvel , as an executive producer on major hits like The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy, Avengers: Age of Ultron , and Spider-Man: Homecoming . He was also part of the team for Iron Man and Iron Man 2 . Since 2017, he has moved into producing other films, with the most recent being the 2026 comedy, The Breadwinner . While that was a commercial and critical flop, Latcham has two excellent movies to his name that signal good things for his tenure with DC Studios.

A year after working as executive producer on Spider-Man: Homecoming , Jeremy Latcham was one of the producers on 2018's Bad Times at the El Royale . The other producer is director/writer Drew Goddard, who put together one of the most underrated films of the 2010s. The neo-noir thriller doubles as a mystery story that centers on several strangers who come together at the titular El Royale hotel, located on the California-Nevada border. What follows is a barrage of secrets and murder, setting up themes of faith and morality.

Bad Times at the El Royale has a stellar cast that includes Jeff Bridges, Cynthia Erivo, Dakota Johnson, Jon Hamm, Cailee Spaeny, Lewis Pullman, and Nick Offerman, just to name a few. Chris Hemsworth steals the show in a more villainous role than we're used to from him, setting the tone for his excellent performance years later in Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga . Bad Times at the El Royale bombed at the box office but received strong reviews and is already finding its footing as a modern cult classic that deserves more love. The same could be said for the movie Latcham produced next.

In 2023, Latcham was a producer on Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves . Thanks to the popularity of the game, this film grossed over $200 million worldwide, but with a budget of $150 million, it is considered a flop. That's a shame because it's actually a really fun interpretation of D&D that was a critical darling, sitting at 91% on Rotten Tomatoes. Chris Pine, Michelle Rodriguez, Sophia Lillis, and the rest of the cast brought a ton of energy to this fantasy story and it should've spawned a huge franchise. Alas, potential sequels are unlikely given the film's financial struggles.

There are many who are worried about DC Studios with Jeremy Latcham at the helm and that's understandable. Even if you didn't like everything Gunn was doing with DC, he clearly had a vision and after the debacle of the Zack Snyder era, fans just wanted to see something delivered to completion. Whatever the end result will be of Latcham's tenure, his resume is promising. Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves takes something established and does something interesting with it, which bodes well for DC and its many popular properties.

If they can deliver something unexpected and fresh, it would go a long way towards people finding new confidence in DC movies. Meanwhile, if you look at Bad Times at the El Royale alongside Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves , it's clear that Latcham movies know how to put together a good cast. These films have a tremendous blend of established veteran performers (Hemsworth, Erivo, Pine, Rodriguez) and rising stars (Spaeny, Pullman, Lillis, Justice Smith). That's a formula that has worked for the MCU in the past and sounds good for DC.

There's also Jeremy Latcham's Marvel credentials to consider. Similar to James Gunn, this is someone who has found success with superhero projects in the past. He knows what it takes to make hits like The Avengers and Guardians of the Galaxy , so he should be able to apply that to DC. Gunn was already doing that and Latcham needs to follow in those footsteps to make this a successful venture. If his DC films are as good as Bad Times at the El Royale and Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves , he'll likely achieve that.

What are your thoughts on these great Jeremy Latcham films? Let us know in the comments!

Vishal Chaturvedi's hit " Hanuman Ansh " and Vinod Kapri's " Pyre " will headline a pop-up inflatable cinema at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa, where the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG) have teamed with PictureTime Digiplex again.

The mobile auditorium is going up on the Kala Academy campus and will serve as a festival hub, screening films every day from Nov. 21 to Nov. 28. The program is split into three strands: Contemporary, Children's Films and Nostalgia. Alongside "Hanuman Ansh" and "Pyre," the contemporary selection includes Deepti Pillay Sivan's Malayalam-language "Achappa's Album" and Sachin Mohite's Marathi-language "Kapuskoonda."

"Our association with NFDC and IFFI has grown into a meaningful, long-standing partnership, and it is always special for us to return to a festival that brings together the best of Indian and international cinema," said Sushil Chaudhary, founder and CEO of PictureTime Digiplex.

Shah Rukh Khan romances dominate the Nostalgia section. Yash Chopra's "Darr: A Violent Love Story," "Dil To Pagal Hai," "Jab Tak Hai Jaan" and "Veer Zaara" will play along with Aditya Chopra's "Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge." Kunal Kohli's "Fanaa" and two Nasir Hussain films, "Yaadon Ki Baarat" and "Hum Kisise Kum Naheen," round out the strand.

On the children's side, Kaushal Oza's 2026 film "Little Thomas," with Gulshan Devaiah and Rasika Dugal in the cast and Ranjan Singh among its co-producers, will anchor the morning screenings for schoolchildren. Other family titles include Sai Paranjpye's "Bhago Bhoot" (2000), Rajeev Sharma's "Bandu Boxer" (2006), Rajan Khosa's "Gattu" (2011), Batul Mukhtiar's "Kaphal-Wild Berries" (2013) and Pankuj Parashar's "Banarasi Jasoos" (2015). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Chaudhary added: "What makes this edition especially exciting is the range of audiences and cinematic experiences we are looking to bring together. … Equally important for us is extending the festival experience beyond its core venues and delegates, and bringing these films to local communities across Goa so that they too can participate in and feel a part of IFFI."

The Goa run caps a busy year for the company. PictureTime also supported the exhibition infrastructure at the Dharamshala International Film Festival and took "Pyre" to audiences in the Indian hinterland.

articles.title: 29 Years Later, Dragon Ball Ended Its Controversial 64-Episode Long Series That Fans Still Don't Appreciate
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation For quite some time, many shonen fans believed that Dragon Ball GT would always be seen as the “Black Sheep” of the Z-Fighters’ franchise. Luckily, Dragon Ball Daima took quite a few elements from the Grand Tour in order to add some serious excitement to the original anime story. Goku went Super Saiyan 4 for the first time in […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google For quite some time, many shonen fans believed that Dragon Ball GT would always be seen as the “Black Sheep” of the Z-Fighters’ franchise. Luckily, Dragon Ball Daima took quite a few elements from the Grand Tour in order to add some serious excitement to the original anime story. Goku went Super Saiyan 4 for the first time in continuity, and Vegeta did the same with Super Saiyan 3, scratching off a major item from many anime fans’ bucket lists. Though Dragon Ball GT is an odd installment in the franchise, its villains are unique, and their power scale is off the charts. GT being labeled an odd and non-canon series became more common after Dragon Ball Super debuted.

With the latest installment, Dragon Ball Daima , incorporating some of GT ’s best elements and making them partially canon, such as Goku’s Super Saiyan 4, GT may now feel narratively redundant. That said, the series is far from a bad installment, as it features many strong elements, including some of the franchise’s best villains. While the Shadow Dragons stand as some of the strongest villains in the entire franchise outside of Super , there are two other uniquely powerful antagonists as well.

GT ’s most defining decision is turning Goku back into a kid and sending him on a space spanning hunt for the Black Star Dragon Balls. It was a deliberate attempt to pull the series back toward the playful, exploratory tone of early  Dragon Ball . It also signals that the show wants to be a journey again, which matches Toriyama’s own explanation of the “Grand Touring” idea.

The problem is not that the premise is invalid. The problem is that the execution struggles to generate momentum. The early stretch can feel like it is searching for the exact blend of comedy, adventure, and stakes that made the original so breezy. Meanwhile, the audience is carrying  Z  in their bones, where tension tends to build through clear escalation.  GT  asks viewers to trade that for episodic wandering, then occasionally asks them to care like it is still  Z . Some fans love that throwback ambition. Others experience it as a stall, because the show has not yet earned the slower pace with enough charm or focus.

If  GT  has a stretch that makes its existence feel justified, it is the Baby saga. Baby is not simply another strong opponent. The idea ties directly into Saiyan history through the Tuffles and reframes “Saiyan pride” into something with consequences. The possession element also gives the arc a different kind of tension, because the threat spreads through characters you already care about. It is not only about whether Goku can win. It is about whether the world around him can be recovered.

This is also where  Super Saiyan 4  arrives, and it remains  GT ’s most enduring contribution.  SSJ4  looks like a return to something older and wilder, pulling from Great Ape imagery and Saiyan roots. Even people who bounce off  GT  often admit  SSJ4  is a striking idea, and it has stayed alive in games and merchandise for a reason.

GT was always going to be judged harshly. But it also proves that Dragon Ball can survive reinterpretation, but it also proves that continuation is not just a matter of having more enemies to fight. It is a matter of voice. So yes, it is polarizing. But polarizing is not the same as empty. Thirty years after Feb. 7, 1996, GT remains the franchise’s most instructive sequel .

Do you think Dragon Ball GT deserves more appreciation despite the fan backlash? Which part of the series do you think holds up best today? Share your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Did Anthony Mackie Spoil Avengers: Doomsday Cameo? Marvel Star Sets the Record Straight
articles.summary: Captain America is known for his stoicism in the face of danger and strong leadership during a crisis, but Anthony Mackie should stay clear of adding loose lips to that list of characteristics. Last week, the Avengers star may have leaked some information about the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday film in an interview with Entertainment Tonight, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Captain America is known for his stoicism in the face of danger and strong leadership during a crisis, but Anthony Mackie should stay clear of adding loose lips to that list of characteristics. Last week, the Avengers star may have leaked some information about the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday film in an interview with Entertainment Tonight , but this on-screen superhero didn't have the proper SHIELD clearance to officially drop that information. Since then, there has been a ton of confusion over his remarks, leading to more rumors and innuendo about who might be showing up when Doctor Doom arrives to challenge the MCU.

Mackie isn't the first performer in this franchise to ruffle feathers over saying things he shouldn't be. In the past, Tom Holland has been relied on by journalists to mention something he shouldn't be saying out loud. Mark Ruffalo has also been in hot water for doing the same after nearly spoiling the surprise ending of Infinity War back in 2018. Someone has to hold these actors accountable for their words, and a certain talk show host decided to ask the former Falcon to clarify his statement and help us understand precisely what he was talking about when he may or may not have spoiled something huge in Doomsday .

Mackie appeared earlier this week on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon to talk about many things including his return to Broadway to play Macbeth in 2027, but the primary focus was Avengers: Doomsday and how Sam Wilson fits into the movie . Fallon wasted no time by showing his receipts and reminding the audience that Mackie may have let a surprise Doomsday reveal slip in his recent interview with ET. In that video, Mackie explained how it was like a "summer camp" vibe being around so many stars at once, and was excited to say “I got to hang out with, you know, Paul Bettany, who I love.” Vision hasn't been confirmed to be in the movie yet, so the rumor mill went into action immediately.

"Paul Bettany is my man, my homie; we hang out all the time," Mackie told Fallon during his appearance. "He was shooting VisionQuest next door to where we were shooting Avengers . So, me being me, I steal a golf cart and pull up. I'm a pull-upper… So I didn't say he was in Doomsday , I said he was next door shooting his show. Just like Tom Holland was next door shooting Spider-Man . He was next door! He wasn't in the movie… I guess?"

Mackie's attempt at damage control left the audience at home and in the studio with even more questions than it did answers, and that was likely all a part of this stunt. Whether Mackie had always intended to leak this information or was now forced to save face with this appearance we may never know, but at the very least we know his words have neither confirmed or denied anything in a concrete way. We're back to square one, with some cautiously optimistic that Vision could appear in Doomsday … but he could also be sitting this one out.

Paul Bettany has remained silent about his potential role in Doomsday , and has said nary a word about the topic. “I’m just trying to keep the kids in shoes and if I tell you that, I’ll get fired," Bettany told Good Morning America during an appearance in October. "I’m just out there hustling.” We do have several confirmations about who we will see when the movie arrives in theaters on Dec. 18, including the Fantastic Four's Sue Storm in a new costume . Everything else is speculation for now, but with less than a month away before showtime we won't have long before we get all the answers we hoped for and many more we weren't expecting.

Do you think it makes sense for Vision to appear in Doomsday , or are there plenty of other characters who are more important to the plot? Join the conversation and let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Is Billy Maximoff in Avengers: Doomsday? Marvel Star Responds After VisionQuest Tease
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel With VisionQuest ending on the possible family reunion of the Maximoff twins, Billy Kaplan actor Joe Locke has spoken out about whether fans will see him in Avengers: Doomsday. Locke debuted in Agatha All Along as a teenage Billy Kaplan, a young man who inherited the soul of Billy Maximoff after Kaplan's death. Locke returned […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With VisionQuest ending on the possible family reunion of the Maximoff twins, Billy Kaplan actor Joe Locke has spoken out about whether fans will see him in Avengers: Doomsday . Locke debuted in Agatha All Along as a teenage Billy Kaplan, a young man who inherited the soul of Billy Maximoff after Kaplan's death. Locke returned in the VisionQuest season finale, which was a big deal since Ruaridh Mollica debuted as Thomas Shepherd, the young man whose body Tommy Maximoff's soul ended up in. Locke talked about the chance for a full family reunion while appearing on The View .

According to Locke, "Marvel brings characters back all the time, and you never know when you’re going to see them, like Wanda." While this teases a return to the MCU, he stopped short of saying he was coming back, and Marvel has not announced that Billy would return anytime soon.

Will Wiccan Be Back in the MCU for Avengers: Doomsday ? Image Courtesy of Marvel There is a slim chance that Joe Locke could be back as Billy in Avengers: Doomsday . It might be better for Marvel to wait until Avengers: Secret Wars to bring in Billy and Tommy. The reason for waiting is simple. If Wanda is coming back in Avengers: Doomsday to help Doctor Doom build Battleworld, there has to be a way to redeem her in the next movie, after everything she has done wrong. This could play into what happened in the Secret Wars miniseries, where Reed Richards was able to turn Molecule Man against Doctor Doom to get the upper hand.

It would make more sense with Wanda if she were serving Doctor Doom because of her anger stemming from losing everything and being stopped from taking her children back in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness . There might not be a better way for her to return to the side of good than by reuniting with Vision, Tommy, and Billy during Avengers: Secret Wars . Learning they are still alive could be the perfect turning point. Bringing Billy back early in Avengers: Doomsday would ruin that possible twist.

That said, it is almost certain that Joe Locke will eventually be back in the MCU because of the rumors of an upcoming Champions movie. That movie would feature teenage heroes like Kamala Khan, Ironheart, and Kate Bishop. Wiccan and Speed (Tommy) are now in the MCU, and the heart and soul of the team could easily be Wiccan and Hulkling, a herothe MCU still needs to introduce to complete this team . Wiccan and Hulkling's relationship is one of the best in Marvel Comics, and not bringing it to the MCU would be a huge mistake. Even if Wiccan doesn't show up in the two Avengers movies, he will be back soon. That much is certain.

articles.title: The Batman's Most Clever Twist Fooled Even Comic Book Readers & It Could Set Up the Sequel
articles.summary: Matt Reeves used Dark Knight fans' knowledge about the comics against them in The Batman. The director took a famous revelation from Batman: Hush and tricked comics readers into thinking they knew exactly where the movie was going and flipped their expectations on their head. The 2022 film is packed with references to Batman’s comic […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Matt Reeves used Dark Knight fans' knowledge about the comics against them in The Batman . The director took a famous revelation from Batman: Hush and tricked comics readers into thinking they knew exactly where the movie was going and flipped their expectations on their head. The 2022 film is packed with references to Batman’s comic book history, but this one actually plays a role in how the story unfolds.

The trick is in the film’s last act, after the Riddler is captured and Batman visits him in Arkham. Paul Dano’s Edward Nashton seems delighted to meet the Dark Knight, thinking that they’ve been working together to uproot the corruption of Gotham. But then he starts repeating Bruce Wayne’s name, and suddenly Batman has a much bigger problem on his hands. For anyone familiar with Jeph Loeb and Jim Lee’s Batman: Hush , the scene feels like it’s building to some sort of revelation about Batman’s secret identity. Reeves knows exactly what those viewers were hoping for.

Batman: Hush introduced Thomas Elliot , a childhood friend of Bruce Wayne who becomes the villain known as Hush. Elliot constructs a conspiracy that involves nearly every major member of Batman's rogues' gallery, but the real puppet master is the Riddler. In Batman #619, Batman faces off against Edward Nygma, who explains that he discovered Bruce Wayne’s secret identity after using a Lazarus Pit to cure his terminal cancer. Batman flips the script, saying that a riddle that everyone knows the answer to isn't much of a riddle. Riddler’s obsession with having to prove he’s smart is the thing that stops him from giving Batman’s identity up.

Reeves drops a conspicuous Hush reference early in his film. As the Wayne family’s secrets are revealed by the Riddler, audiences learn that Thomas Wayne went to Carmine Falcone to have a reporter named Edward Elliot silenced. Falcone kills the journalist, and the word “HUSH” appears on the screen during the Riddler’s presentation. The reference gives comic readers reason to think that the Riddler has discovered Batman's identity, just as he did in Hush . Their suspicions seem confirmed when Nashton keeps chanting “Bruce Wayne” at Arkham.

Except the Riddler does not know that Bruce Wayne is Batman. He’s angry that Wayne survived the attempt on his life, and he resents the sympathy that Bruce got as a rich orphan, while kids like Nashton suffered in Gotham’s forgotten orphanage. Riddler is convinced that Batman has been aiding him in exposing the city’s corruption, not that he’s been sitting across from the billionaire he tried to kill. What Reeves did was use a revelation that comic readers already knew to make them expect a twist that never happened. The deception worked because they knew Hush .

The Hush references could have another payoff in the sequel. The first film's murdered reporter, Edward Elliot shares a surname with the comic book villain and has a first name similar to Nashton, suggesting that Elliot could be Riddler’s father. Asked about the theory by The Hollywood Reporter , co-writer Peter Craig said, “The way that you’re reading it would make some people, including Matt Reeves, very happy.” “We've discussed related details in development, but we're not going to give anything away, as that would ruin future plans,” Craig added that related details had been discussed during development. He refused to say more to avoid spoiling future plans.

Reeves has also expressed an interest in bringing Hush into his Batman universe , but warned against expecting the character to show up in the sequel. Most recently, Reeves has teased that The Batman Part II will explore Bruce Wayne’s past and introduce a villain who has not yet appeared in a live-action Batman movie. That’s kept Hush among the popular theories, though James Gunn has pushed back against rumors claiming to know the sequel’s villain.

Robert Pattinson returns as Bruce Wayne in The Batman Part II , co-starring Colin Farrell, Andy Serkis, and Jeffrey Wright. Newcomers include Scarlett Johansson, Sebastian Stan and Charles Dance. Filming had taken a short break recently, but is back on with Oscar-winning director Steven Soderbergh stepping in to help finish filming while Reeves deals with a family matter. The sequel is scheduled to arrive on February 18th, 2028 . We’ll see if the Elliot connection pans out or if Reeves has some other trick up his sleeve, but the first movie proved just how well he knows the comic book history of Batman. He didn't need the Riddler to find out Batman's secret identity. All he needed was comic book fans to think he had.

articles.title: 'Much Ado About Nothing' Broadway Review: Tom Hiddleston, Hayley Atwell & Jamie Lloyd Throw An Irresistible Party Of Shakespeare's Great Comedy
articles.summary: Outside of ticker tape parades and New Year's Eve in Times Square, you might be hard-pressed to think of a better, more joyous use of floating paper than the confetti that piles up nightly on the stage of Broadway's Winter Garden Theatre these days. We're talking blizzards of the pink stuff, so deep that the […]
articles.content:
Outside of ticker tape parades and New Year's Eve in Times Square, you might be hard-pressed to think of a better, more joyous use of floating paper than the confetti that piles up nightly on the stage of Broadway 's Winter Garden Theatre these days. We're talking blizzards of the pink stuff, so deep that the man known for playing that Marvel trickster Loki can all but bury his superhero frame in the drifts.

The new, infectious Much Ado About Nothing , Jamie Lloyd 's inventive and joyous revival of the Shakespeare comedy opening tonight at the Winter Garden, turns those old falling drifts of thin paper into a special effect that, for sheer exuberance, more than holds its own against the cutting-edge projections and awesome digital flimflammery delighting audiences at any number of Broadway houses this season. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Josh Radnor & Beth Behrs To Join Broadway's 'Schmigadoon!' News Jonathan Spector's Acclaimed 'Birthright' Sets Spring Broadway Opening

Of course, even a confetti squall such as this wouldn't impress a lick if the rest of Lloyd's production couldn't match its energy, and fortunately for us all this Much Ado About Nothing never lacks for giddy enchantment, from the Tony-worthy performances of stars Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell to the irresistible choreography of Fabian Aloise that will likely leave audiences of this straight play convinced they've just witnessed one of the best new musicals on Broadway this season. Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

Hiddleston, with his charm level cranked, and Atwell, best known to moviegoers for her Agent Carter of Marvel fame and here matching her fellow superhero beat for beat, play Benedick and Beatrice, two of Shakespeare's most delightful characters, Loki-level tricksters who, as another character notes, engage in a "merry war" of plotting, planning and scheming in the name of love (though neither would admit to that motive, at least early on).

Lloyd, whose typically stark theatrical approach if on full view here but utilized to an effect wholly different than the shadows-and-light desolation of his A Doll's House (starring Jessica Chastain) or Betrayal (which also paired him with Hiddleston), fashions this foray into Shakespeare as a 1990s-era dance club - at one point, the entire cast dons oversized, mascot-style headpieces (a chick, an octopus, a dog, a robot and more) suggesting so many ecstasy-fueled club kids packed into the Limelight. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The plot, of course, is the usual Shakespearean farce full of disguised identities, battles of the sexes, intricate schemes and star-crossed romances both helped and hindered by busybodies, eavesdroppers and nefarious in-laws. (In Shakespeare's day, the word "nothing" carried a double meaning: In addition to our understood definition, "nothing" in its ye olde pronunciation carried a near-pun on the word "noting," or gossip).

While productions of Shakespeare have long been interpreted with any number of contemporary spins and modern touches - such are the stock in trade of New York's Shakespeare in the Park - Lloyd has come up with an approach that feels entirely fresh: Hiddleston, Atwell, the wonderful Mason Alexander Park and the rest of the cast move and sing to such jubilant dance and pop hits as Taylor Dayne's "Tell It to My Heart," C & C Music Factory's "Gonna Make You Sweat (Everybody Dance Now)," Deee-Lite's "Groove Is in the Heart," and All-4-One's "I Swear." I knew we were in for a treat when Hiddleston's Benedick and his boy crew made an entrance dancing to the Beastie Boys' booming "Fight for Your Right (To Party)."

If period drama set to a more-or-less contemporary soundtrack doesn't sound all that innovative - Six and Moulin Rouge! would like a word - Lloyd and his crack creative team (and his cast, of course) see to it that we pretty much forget all other contenders. With that ever-present pink confetti, a giant inflatable heart, character-accentuating modern dress (Soutra Gilmour did both the scenic design and the party-wear costume designs) and Jon Clark's gorgeous lighting combine to create a dazzling experience. Like any dance club worth its cover charge, the sound design (by Ben and Max Ringham) is practically a showstopper in itself, with music thumping when it needs to thump and, when we need to hear dialogue, dropping to the sort of low-level thrum you might hear on the curb outside a packed club.

Hiddleston, whose last team-up with Lloyd was the austere Betrayal , is a revelation here, adding some incredibly hot dance moves to his overflowing bag of tricks. And he's very, very funny (watch how he ever so deadpan blows a bit of stray confetti from his lips), playing off his movie star appeal with every sidelong glance and knowing grin seemingly directed to each person in the audience (he's not above a quick show of gratitude when his seated admirers whoop their appreciation, as if his Benedick is welcoming everyone into his scheming maneuvers).

Atwell is every bit his equal, with Beatrice's fiery, feminist mettle rendered as the true heart and brains of this tale. Both actor and role are this productions not-so-secret weapons - and yes, Lloyd and his cast are entirely in on the Marvel appeal going on here, so much so that Hiddleston-as-Loki and Atwell-as-Carter make brief appearances in the form of standees that had the audience at the reviewed performance all but levitating.

As good as they are - and they are - newcomer (to American audiences anyway) Mason Alexander Park as the sharp-tongued Margaret nearly walks off with the show, never more so than when, mic in hand, she/they performs "Tell It To My Heart" as if placing a dance-pop diva in 16th Century Milan is no more strange than wooing your heart's desire.

Indeed, there's no weak link in this cast, with James Phoon's callow young Claudio swoon-worthy when he needs to be, infuriating when he's a jerk; Tim Steed's meddlesome Don John a hissable villain; and Gerald Kyd's Don Pedro - that fair-weather father to the slandered Hero (a winning Mara Huf) - an appropriately garrulous, welcoming host (until he isn't). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

The grand appeal of this production is evident in just how much Hiddleston, Atwell and their compatriots seem to be enjoying themselves, and why not? So is everyone within the clarion-call-to-groove of those thumping, galvanizing dance beats.

Title: Much Ado About Nothing Venue: Broadway’s Winter Garden Theatre Written By: Willliam Shakespeare Directed By: Jamie Lloyd Cast: Tom Hiddleston, Hayley Atwell, Mara Huf, Mika Onyx Johnson, Gerald Kyd, Forbes Masson, Phillip Olagoke, Mason Alexander Park, James Phoon, Tim Steed Running Time: 2 hr 20 min (including intermission)

articles.title: 'War' Stars Sienna Miller and Dominic West Tussle Over Who Won the Divorce Drama: 'Gwyneth Paltrow Ran So That the Rest of Us Could Walk'
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “War,” which had its season finale on Nov. 19 on HBO and HBO Max in the U.S., and drops on Nov. 20 on Sky and NOW in the U.K. The climactic season finale of “War”—  the Sky and HBO drama series starring Sienna Miller and Dominic West […]
articles.content:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “War,” which had its season finale on Nov. 19 on HBO and HBO Max in the U.S., and drops on Nov. 20 on Sky and NOW in the U.K.

The climactic season finale of “War”—  the Sky and HBO drama series starring Sienna Miller and Dominic West as warring spouses — sees an unexpected denouement just as the couple's increasingly bitter divorce is about to be finalized. With their lawyers still battling it out, the couple bury the hatchet and hammer out their own, more equitable deal. And with that, they walk off into the sunset.

Written and created by by George Kay (“Hijack”), the series is set to return for a second season with a new case — and new clients — to occupy the show’s fictional law firms, Taylor & Byrne and Cathcarts. In Season 2, Marisa Tomei, Kelly Macdonald and David Harewood join the cast as the litigants in a high-stakes defamation case.

While Miller and West won’t reprise their roles as actress Carla Duvall and tech billionaire Morgan Henderson, neither seems quite ready to leave their characters behind. In a chat with Variety , both actors repeatedly slipped back into their roles, cheerily arguing over Morgan’s “flirting” with Carla’s barrister (Celia Imrie), Carla’s dalliance with Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux) and who really won their explosive — extremely expensive — divorce battle.

Read on for the full conversation. Related Stories 'Heartland' Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir ‘Steps’ Review: Brightly Colored, Harmless Reimagining of ‘Cinderella’ Packs Funny Lines but Little That's Unique

Sienna Miller: It was the last thing we ever shot, so that was lovely. And I can't really remember: A part of me probably wanted something really dramatic and cataclysmic to happen. But at the same time, I defer to the brilliance of George Kay knowing what an audience wants, because he's written the show that people are devouring. I think the sensationalist in me wanted handbags at dawn [ British idiom meaning “a dramatic showdown” ], but I also in retrospect think it's quite lovely that they had that moment. Dom?

Dominic West: "Handbags at dawn" — that would have been great. I'd have loved handbags at dawn.

Miller: I think George told us that essentially, this is what's going to happen: The lawyers screw everything up, and [Carla and Morgan] got there in a much more simple way. So we had an idea — not at the beginning of shooting, but as we were going on — we're like, “How does it end? What happens?!” You know, nagging like a bunch of kids. We had an inkling that that was what it was, but, again, I was 35 weeks pregnant, so the whole thing is a blur. That's why I'm hoping Dom can jump in.

West: I remember my first thoughts were “Fucking hell, what a waste of £10 million” or whatever they spent on the lawyers when they just make it up between themselves. But actually, I think that was the point George was trying to make, and I quite like the idea that they had to go through this terrible process of lawyers and courtroom drama and going to war with each other basically in order to realize actually what they meant to each other. And how they could amicably come to an arrangement where both felt that they'd got what they deserved, and that their relationship had been quantified in a good way, in a just way.

But I think that's the thing that really hit me was “What a fucking waste of £10 million.” But then, if you're a billionaire, I suppose you do waste £10 million quite happily just to work out how much you like your ex-wife or ex-husband.

Miller: I do think there's something very zeitgeist-y — and I'm not sure how he's done this, George — but the timing of this show is so interesting. I read an article, and it was talking about “Just normalize divorce.” That the process of divorce has become so acrimonious, hellish. The children suffer. It should be something that can be amicable. Obviously, Gwyneth Paltrow ran so that the rest of us could walk. But there is a conscious uncoupling that can be lovely and better for everyone, and it left it left me feeling that it probably should be the goal to avoid conflict and remember why you love this person and how to end it in the nicest way.

West: No, we didn’t. But [Kay] didn't tell us straight away, did he? I don't think I knew that it was going to end so amicably.

Miller: I still think I won in court.

West: I don’t think you did, dear.

Miller: Well, I think the audience might feel that I did because you couldn't remember the fucking poem, could you?

West: Well, I suppose you won in that you got money for ideas and running a business that you had nothing to do with. So in that way, I suppose you were a winner.

Miller: I hope that, because [Kay] has left it amicable at the end that Dom and I can pop back.

West: What, a spinoff with Sienna and Johnny? No way!

Miller: Have you watched it, Dom?

West: I haven't watched it all yet. I've only just got Sky, but I'm getting to it. I can't wait. I watched the first episode six times, and I haven't managed to see the rest. But I'm on it.

Miller: One of the cast texted me something very funny, which was “I hope you can come back, but Carla's such a crazy bitch, you never know she might do something else to get in there.”

West: She’s bound to have more legal trouble.

Miller: Well, judging by your nefarious behavior in Episode 1, I think it's coming for you too. Now it's a hit, we really want to be invited back.

Miller: Sorry, we haven’t spoken in a while!

West: It may have ended amicably on set, but it hasn't really ended amicably between Sienna and I in terms of the characters.

West: It was really noticeable in court: When I was talking Sienna was sitting right there, and so we're very close to each other, we can look at each other in the eye. And it was quite thrilling to be putting the boot in, or trying to make war with someone, when you're sitting right there. I was getting into the moment, and that was quite thrilling, to be so confrontational and to be having a go at Carla, with her being right there. The second thing was being cross-examined by Celia Imrie was quite flirty. In fact, very flirty. She was really flirty, Celia.

Miller: You say that about everyone, Dom. I think it might be you.

West: No, no, that was — it was —

Miller: One thing I particularly love about when Dom answers a question about “War” is he always says “to be at war with each other.” You always drop the name, which I appreciate. I just had to say.

West : Yeah, no, good. But anyway, let me finish. So yeah, [Imrie] was quite flirty, but that was her strategy and it was in the writing. But Celia really has got such a twinkle that I loved being cross-examined by her.

Miller: Well, I have been cross-examined [in real life] a few times, I think. I'm pretty sure I have been. Archie Panjabi [who plays Morgan's barrister] was amazing and quite stern, and I had horrible flu that day, so again, an unhelpful, blurry response. I feel like Carla felt so in-the-right in herself that I wasn't particularly rattled. It was an intimidating environment and it was a long day, but I quite enjoyed it because I felt like I had the upper hand. Dom would disagree.

Miller: I mean, I definitely have experienced opening the door and being faced with what Carla is faced with. Not anymore, thank God. But I only read the first script when I signed on. So you’re taking a gamble. I mean, I knew she was an actress and I knew she was famous, so I assumed there might be some of that, but I didn't really — I don't think I want to play an actress again. Unless it's Carla coming back in “War.”

Miller: Not particularly, no, because I didn't know where it would all go or the spins that it would take. And no, it's not particularly interesting for me to relive those moments or those years, but I do have an innate knowledge of them, and I suppose that's interesting for people to see. I feel like I'm so different to Carla herself that maybe her response was an interesting thing to explore. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

West: Yeah, I mean, I suppose I did have hesitations about it, but in practice, in doing it, what was quite thrilling was the thought of a billionaire getting the sort of scrutiny that the British press normally reserves for young actresses. I found that quite a thrill.

This interview has been edited and condensed.

articles.title: 4 More Roles Robert Pattinson Would Be Perfect For, Including One That Would Drive Twilight Fans Wild
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond has been the biggest story in entertainment news this week. It's not just the fact that Pattinson is now playing James Bond and Batman at the same time: anyone who is a fan of cinema knows that Pattinson is currently on a generational run as an actor, with four […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond has been the biggest story in entertainment news this week. It's not just the fact that Pattinson is now playing James Bond and Batman at the same time : anyone who is a fan of cinema knows that Pattinson is currently on a generational run as an actor, with four of his films releasing this year alone ( The Drama, The Odyssey, Primetime, Dune: Part Three ). Pattinson has also become one of the most viral memes since his Bond casting was announced, with the common thread being that he may literally pop in any and every movie role there is, at this point.

But while the internet may be joking about Robert Pattinson snatching up roles like Infinity Stones, we're dead serious about these four particular big roles we think he'd be great for. Keeping with his track record, the roles are either big-star vehicles in established IPs – with one being a high-profile biopic role no one would see coming.

Robert Pattinson has cultivated a wide range of screen personas, and there's no better showcase than a remake of The Nutty Professor . Two comedic greats (Jerry Lewis and Eddie Murphy) have starred in versions of The Nutty Professor (1963 and 1996, respectively); if Robert Pattinson wants to prove he has the comedy genre in the bag, this is a fast lane to do it.

Of course, Pattinson, being the actor that he is, we would expect that a modern flip on The Nutty Professor would be examining the character and themes from a deeper angle than Lewis and Murphy did. In the era of the "Manosphere," where the entire idea of masculinity is a hot-button issue of the Culture Wars, Pattinson could truly embody both sides of the character by delivering a performance that's both smart and funny.

The real start of Robert Pattinson's comeback run was in 2017, when he helped put brothers Josh and Benny Safdie on the map with their crime thriller Good Time . Pattinson shocked cinephiles with his performance as Constantine "Connie" Nikas, a small-time crook and bank robber trying to steal enough money to get his special-needs brother out bonded out of lock-up. Pattinson playing a ne'er-do-well captivated audiences, and that's why he's the perfect pick to help Disney revitalize the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise.

The Jack Sparrow character is the heart of the PotC films, and so far Johnny Depp has had a stranglehold on that performance. However, Pattinson has made it known that he isn't above swiping another actor's job, and he may be the only one with the talent and charisma necessary to replace Depp. A formative prequel story about a younger Jack Sparrow would be great; Pattinson would be a perfect pick for a film where we see Jack go from being a meek, naive civilian to becoming the cunning, bold, tanned, jewel-adorned pirate in heavy makeup and a signature bandana we know and love.

Only the most angular face in cinema can play the most angular face in professional sports – I said it, and I stand on it. Seeing Pattinson take on Chris Hansen Primetime opened up whole new career possibilities for him, at least in my mind: biopics done in artistically bold ways we don't expect. Pattinson has overcome doubts about his physicality when playing Batman, and will face similar criticisms as he's gearing up to play Bond. But if he overcomes the naysayers twice, then playing one of the greatest sports specimens ever will seem much more realistic. Every actor has that one role that demands an almost unthinkable physical transformation: the smart ones usually save it for a biopic that opens a door to awards like the Golden Globes and the Oscars. One photo of Pattinson having stacked and cut muscle to look like Tom Brady, and that biopic film becomes a mainstream discussion overnight.

However, the real intrigue of Pattinson playing Tom Brady wouldn't be the sports action portion of the story (save that for stunt doubles). Pattinson has the offbeat manner necessary for playing up some of Brady's deeper eccentricities, quirks, and vulnerabilities. Brady is notorious for having a diet, workout regimen, and general life view and disciplines that very few other human beings could; Pattinson is the type of actor who could dig into and display the actual man at the center of all the mythic life lore – comedically, dramatically, or a fine mix of both.

Brady has said in the past he wants Leo DiCaprio to play him , but we're betting he'd be pretty satisfied with Pattinson, too.

Want to make all the money in the world? Then circle this whole thing back to when Pattinson first became an international star (and hearthrob) playing Edward Cullen in the Twilight Saga films. Only this time? Do it sexy, cool, and gnarl y.

Dracula is one of the most enduring characters in both literature and cinema; Francis For Coppola's 1992 film, Bram Stoker's Dracula , was a testament to how gorgeous, enticing, and still horrifying and gory a true Gothic-horror-romance adaptation of the Dracula novel could be. That kind of range took a central performer with that same level of range: Coppola had Gary Oldman to pull it off; this generation has Robert Pattinson. From the suave gentleman seducing Mina Harker, to the decript ghoul Jonathan Harker is enslaved by, to the nightmarish creature who feeds on everyone in between, this performance would be Pattinson at max aura .

Going for all the ridicule over Edward to playing the fearsome and charismatic king of all vampires would be the ultimate culimation of this Robert Pattinson run. And all the smart ways he could (would?) troll the haters would be legendary.

Robert Pattinson will likely star as both Bond and Batman in 2028; but first, he'll star as the villain of Dune: Part Three on December 18th. Any of these roles above sound good to you ?

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Grand Theft Auto 6 has a few different camera angles players can choose from, but a first-person perspective isn't one of them. However, that's only officially speaking, as some crafty players have figured out a way to force the game into a first-person viewpoint.

As found by oneboyler and OrangeGuy on YouTube , those who want to put the camera in Jason's or Lucia's eyes have to do a bit of fiddling. First, players have to go into the Controller tab in the settings and change the Touch Pad (PS5) or View button (Xbox Series X|S) so that it changes the camera angle (it defaults to opening the map).

From there, get into a car and pull out your phone by pressing up on the D-pad. Put the phone away with the Circle or B button and then mash the Touchpad or View button. This will probably take a few tries, but, if done correctly, will make the game playable with a first-person camera.

This glitch is, unsurprisingly, a little wonky. The protagonist's arms or other appendages can clip through the camera, and it's possible there are other quirks that come up when playing in this mode; the game is huge, after all . However, this unofficial first-person mode is relatively fully featured and behaves like it is a standard setting, meaning players can run around and gun people down in first-person with relative ease.

Changing the camera back to normal is similarly a little tedious. To go back to the default camera angles, players have to reload their save or retry a checkpoint. This means players will have to redo the glitch every time they want to go back to first-person mode (unless it get patched out, which is possible).

It's a little odd that GTA 6 doesn't have a more official first-person mode. Grand Theft Auto 5 didn't have it when it launched on PS3 and Xbox 360 in 2013, but it got its own first-person toggle when it was remastered for PS4, Xbox One, and PC, and it became one of the port's standout new features. Red Dead Redemption 2 , on the other hand, launched with it and let players tackle the Wild West from day one through Arthur Morgan's eyes.

Given that track record, it wouldn't be surprising if GTA 6 gets an official first-person update sometime down the line. The game is still slated to come to PC in the near future , so it's possible Rockstar Games will once again add in first-person mode when the game hits PC. Regardless, it seems likely players will be able to tackle Leonida one day through this more intimate perspective.

Are you going to play GTA 6 in first-person through this glitch? Or are you going to wait for something more official? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
After nearly 30 years, the cast of Can't Hardly Wait is ready for a Huntington Hillside High reunion.

Having reprised their roles from the cult classic 1998 teen film for Halloween, Peter Facinelli and Joel Michaely noted that fans "have been clamoring" for them to make a sequel for years, suggesting they make their interest known to Sony Pictures.

articles.title: This Forgotten Sci-Fi Movie Gave Us One of the Most Underrated Alien Invasions in Film History
articles.summary: Most alien invasion movies tend to have a similar playbook. Once giant spaceships appear in Earth's atmosphere, military forces scramble to defend themselves against an inevitable invasion. Usually, a hero or heroes save the day. There's nothing wrong with that. I love a good alien invasion spectacle as much as anybody. But what if the extraterrestrials […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Most alien invasion movies tend to have a similar playbook. Once giant spaceships appear in Earth's atmosphere, military forces scramble to defend themselves against an inevitable invasion. Usually, a hero or heroes save the day. There's nothing wrong with that. I love a good alien invasion spectacle as much as anybody. But what if the extraterrestrials didn't bother announcing themselves? What if they were already here, quietly changing the world around us while the rest of humanity went about its business? That's a considerably creepier idea, and one forgotten science fiction movie had a lot of fun exploring it.

Released in 1996, this Charlie Sheen thriller took a different approach to the usual extraterrestrial invasion story. Instead of giving us another Independence Day-style battle for the planet, it imagined something much more insidious. The aliens weren't necessarily interested in blowing up our cities. They wanted to take over without attracting attention. Thirty years later, the movie's central idea still makes for a fascinating piece of science fiction . And there's a pretty good reason it deserves another look.

The Arrival follows Zane Zaminsky, an astronomer played by Charlie Sheen who discovers a strange signal coming from deep space. Naturally, he does what any curious scientist would do. He digs deeper into things. Unfortunately, his discovery puts him on the radar of some very dangerous people. Next thing he knows, Zane finds himself involved in a conspiracy that stretches much further than he could have imagined. The really interesting part is what he discovers. The aliens aren't waiting for humanity to notice them. They've already established themselves on Earth, and they've been working on something much bigger than a simple visit.

That's what makes the movie's invasion so unsettling. Director David Twohy doesn't rely on enormous spacecraft hovering over New York or armies of extraterrestrials marching through the streets. Instead, he builds the story around the possibility that the people running parts of our world might not be human at all. It's a wonderfully paranoid premise, especially when Zane starts realizing how difficult it is to convince anybody that something extraordinary is happening. Sheen makes for an entertaining lead because Zane isn't some unstoppable action hero. He's a scientist who stumbles into something terrifying and has to figure out what to do with the information. There's a little bit of The X-Files in the whole affair, which is hardly a bad thing for a 1990s sci-fi thriller.

The Arrival really knew how to get the most mileage out of its relatively simple premise. The movie understands that an alien invasion doesn't necessarily need to involve the destruction of famous landmarks to be frightening. Sometimes the idea that something is happening right under our noses is considerably worse. The aliens have their own agenda, and humanity isn't exactly in a position to negotiate. Twohy also gives the film some memorable science fiction imagery, particularly as Zane gets closer to understanding what the extraterrestrials are doing. The story gets increasingly strange, but it never loses sight of its central mystery. That's an important distinction. Plenty of sci-fi movies have interesting ideas that fall apart once the explanations start arriving. The Arrival manages to keep things entertaining.

The movie also arrived during a particularly enjoyable period for science fiction . The 1990s gave moviegoers everything from Independence Day and Stargate to Contact and The X-Files . But there was also room for smaller stories that approached the subject from a different angle. The Arrival landed somewhere between those two worlds. It had enough action and spectacle to keep things moving, but its real appeal came from the mystery surrounding the invasion. I wouldn't necessarily put it alongside the genre's undisputed classics, but that's not really the point. It's an entertaining little sci-fi thriller with an idea that deserved more attention than it received. And if you've spent the last few decades watching aliens announce their arrival by blowing up the White House, seeing one quietly take over the planet is a refreshing change of pace.

Are you one of the few who still remember this film? If so, let us know your thoughts!

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google An anime with similar vibes to Delicious in Dungeon will premiere next year, and fans would not want to miss it. There’s no denying that Delicious in Dungeon is one of the greatest fantasies of the 2020s. While the manga has already ended, the anime will be returning with a second season in October next year. Fans are already hyped for the anime’s return, especially after the first season reached its conclusion with a major cliffhanger where Laois and his party thought of an unconventional way to save Falin. While fans still have to wait several months before the anime's return, a new fantasy series has also been announced.

Now that 2026 is closer to its end than ever, the 2027 anime series are all set for their premiere. From the lineup so far, it's evident that 2027 will turn out to be another exciting year for anime fans, maybe even better than 2026. However, there's one anime that fans of Delicious in Dungeon need to watch when it premieres. Revealed via a Kadokawa press release, Soara and the House of Monsters gets a new key visual and promotional video. The anime was already announced in July this year, but Kadokawa shared major updates, especially a 2027 release window along with everything else fans need to know for now.

The anime is based on an acclaimed manga by Hidenori Yamaji, which is currently serializing in Shogakukan's manga app Sunday Webry. The new visual and promotional trailer were revealed on November 18th, 2026, to commemorate Good House Day in Japan. The story centers around Soara, a young orphaned girl raised by knights. She is trained to battle monsters that constantly attack the kingdom, but by the time she is old enough to participate in a real battle, peace has been declared in her kingdom. Now that the skills she spent her whole life learning are of no use, Soara begins to search for a new home and a purpose in life.

Just when all hope seemed lost, she encounters Krik, a dwarf and leader of the Monster Architects. Before long, the girl finds herself working with the Monster Architects to build comfortable homes for them. Produced by Felix Film Studio, the anime is being directed by Takaharu Ozaki, best known for Goblin Slayer. The series composition is done by Ayumu Hisao, while the character design is provided by Tomoko Iwasa. The latest cast members were also revealed in the press release, with Reiji Kawashima as Niko and Kenta Miyake as Gansho. The voices behind Soara (Ikumi Hasegawa) and Krik (Ayumu Murase) were already revealed before this latest update.

While both stories have different narrative structures , they have similar settings and an overall vibe. Soara and the House of Monsters has rich world-building that examines how monsters live, adapt, and fit into their environment, rather than simply treating them as foes to defeat. While one anime centers around architecture and the other is mostly about cooking, both are skills that require practical problem-solving and remodeling spaces to suit different monsters. This upcoming anime will be perfect for fans who love fantasy themes and character growth with a slower, slice-of-life rhythm rather than focusing on intense battle actions.

Are you excited to see this upcoming anime bring its own blend of fantasy and adventure to anime? Do you think it could capture the same appeal as Delicious in Dungeon ? Share your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: 5 Overlooked DC Heroes With Powers That Could Change the DC Universe
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics DC has plenty of powerhouses that everyone points to as examples of unparalleled might. The Spectre can bend reality to his whim on his holy mission, and Superboy-Prime can punch reality hard enough to cause retcons the universe over, as two examples off the top of my head. These characters and others have earned the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google DC has plenty of powerhouses that everyone points to as examples of unparalleled might. The Spectre can bend reality to his whim on his holy mission, and Superboy-Prime can punch reality hard enough to cause retcons the universe over, as two examples off the top of my head. These characters and others have earned the attention, but whenever fans discuss the strongest characters, it's only the most popular characters on those levels who make it. Popularity doesn't dictate strength, and there are plenty of other heroes who can also bring the universe to its knees if they choose to unleash their monstrous power. Today, we're looking at five of those heroes and digging into exactly what makes them so dangerous. So, without further ado, let's dive into DC's obscure demigods.

Sodam Yat's incredible powers are twofold. For one, he's a Daxamite, whose home was a sister planet to Krypton in the same solar system. That means that they have similar powers to Kryptonians. Under the light of a yellow sun, they have the same level os strength, speed, invulnerability, and just about everything else or an equivalent. Already, that makes him as dangerous as someone like Superman or Mon-El. Daxamites have a far more exploitable weakness in lead, which proves fatal no matter how little of the material they come into contact with. Still, that's not much of a concern for Sodam Yat, as he can keep any and all lead away with his Green Lantern ring.

Oh, but Sodam Yat isn't just any Green Lantern. He's the Green Lantern. He was long prophesied to become the greatest Green Lantern of all, his raw talent and willpower earning him the right to become the host for the Entity of Will, Ion. As Ion, he could do practically anything he set his mind to, his usual Green Lantern powers amplified hundreds of times. He could even manipulate time and space to some extent, appearing in multiple places at the same time and teleporting wherever he needed. So, to recap, Sodam Yat is as strong as Superman and as good a Green Lantern as Hal Jordan. I don't think I need to say why that combination is one of the deadliest ones you could possibly ask for.

If you think Tim looks familiar, it's clear that he's DC Harry Potter, which is ironic considering he debuted six years before Harry did. Either way, Tim is destined to become the most powerful mage of all, born as a conduit for raw magic itself, from which Merlin drew his name. He's nowhere near his peak potential yet, still being a child, but don't let that fool you, as he's already monstrously powerful. He's an Opener, meaning that he can subconsciously create entire new parallel universes based on his emotions, which he was subconsciously doing since he was a baby. Once he started to learn about his power, he was able to open gates that not even the combined might of Heaven, Hell, and the Dreaming could do when aided by Earth's best mages.

Even beyond his potent reality manipulation, Tim's magic can do practically anything else he wishes. He can stop or start time at will, hop between dimensions without breaking a sweat, see into the future, control minds, and change into other forms, to name just the tip of the iceberg. Tim has the potential to surpass even the strongest magical minds in reality, from Doctor Fate to Zatanna, and when he reaches his highest level, there won't be anyone who can stop him.

Lor-Zod is, as his name implies, the son of General Zod and Ursa, meaning that he's just as fully Kryptonian as Superman himself. Speaking of the Man of Steel, he was actually adopted by Clark and Lois as a young boy, being named Christopher Kent and raised to be a hero. Funnily enough, he pulled away from his family after being unceremoniously aged up . Sound familiar? Either way, while he's a child again in Prime Earth continuity, in the pre-New 52 world, he was a fully grown Kryptonian. Initially, his powers were weakened a tad due to instabilities from being born in the Phantom Zone. Of course, being on this list means bringing even more than that to the table, and Chris brought it when he merged with the Kryptonian God of Shadows, Nightwing.

As the avatar of Nightwing, also going by the same name, Chris's power was elevated to a whole new level. He has control over shadows and darkness, able to both create constructs akin to a Green Lantern's and an awareness that tells him of anything that happens within darkness. He also sports incredible telekinesis and can teleport practically anywhere, once transporting an entire artificial sun into the Phantom Zone. His upper limits as the avatar of his deity are unknown, but adding anything to Kryptonian strength is more than enough to make him a threat to everyone around.

Kid Eternity is probably the most obscure character on this list. Kitt Freeman is a young man who has demonstrated a ton of powers, but we'll be ignoring most of those one-offs from the Silver Age, instead focusing on his main power, which is the ability to summon spirits from beyond the grave. By shouting "Eternity!" he can make any spirit he imagines appear. They can only stay for a short time, sixty-six seconds, but that is more than enough time for what he needs to do. There are plenty of incredibly powerful figures in DC's history, without a doubt, but the most broken aspect of his power is even stronger. Kitt can not only summon the ghosts of real people, but mythological or even fictional characters.

Imagine the power to make any fictional or mythological character real, even if it was only for a minute at a time. There are some incalculably powerful characters in fiction, with reality-warpers being a dime a dozen if you know where to look. At his peak, Kitt has even summoned entire armies of the deceased to fight alongside him, and can even become a ghost himself, effectively being immortal. Kid Eternity has access to every deceased character in DC, which includes some unfathomably powerful people, without question.

This isn't technically one hero, but rather an item that has been passed down through generations, with the newest users being a young boy named Miguel Montez and an unnamed one-eyed alien. It doesn't matter who has the Hero Dial, as whoever it is has one of the most powerful artifacts ever conceived of in DC. By spelling out the word hero, the user would transform into a random superhero whose power matched the situation they found themself in. Not only could this device transform the wielder into any real superhero, from Superman to the Flash , but it could even turn someone into a hero that doesn't exist, created just for their circumstance.

This item is one of, if not the most broken items in DC, because it gives the user access to literally any and all powers. Heck, the H-Dial would literally let someone transform into anyone else mentioned on this list and then some. The power of Superboy-Prime could belong to a middle-school kid, or an elderly man could turn into Doctor Manhattan at the turn of a dial. The potential of this item is absolutely limitless, and Miguel has shown that he's more than capable of using it to its full extent. This item can make anyone into a hero, and it can turn them into the most powerful hero of all.

Which of these underrated but overpowered heroes would you want to see more of? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Even After 9 Years, This is Still Goku's Best Kamehameha in Dragon Ball Super
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation Dragon Ball has featured its fair share of iconic moments over the decades, but few can come close to Goku's most iconic Kamehameha. While Kamehameha is far from new, it's easily one of the most memorable techniques in all Shonen. Dragon Ball raised entire generations of Shonen fans who grew up watching Goku deliver his […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Dragon Ball has featured its fair share of iconic moments over the decades, but few can come close to Goku's most iconic Kamehameha. While Kamehameha is far from new, it's easily one of the most memorable techniques in all Shonen. Dragon Ball raised entire generations of Shonen fans who grew up watching Goku deliver his most powerful attacks against his opponents. Things changed when the manga received its sequel to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the series' finale. Written by Akira Toriyama and illustrated by Toyotaro, Dragon Ball Super immediately became a massive hit as it introduced its multiverse and a whole new level of power that no one thought was possible.

In Episodes 109 and 110 that were aired as a one-hour special, Goku unlocked his Ultra Instinct , an ability that only deities are capable of using. Also known as the “State of the Gods,” Ultra Instinct allows a user to sever the link between their consciousness and body, allowing them to dodge all kinds of attacks subconsciously. Following the groundbreaking debut of Ultra Instinct, Goku kept using this form through the rest of the tournament. On November 19th, 2017, Dragon Ball Super released Episode 116 in Japan, where Goku used the most powerful Kamehameha in the entire series.

Jiren wasn't the only powerful opponent Goku and the others had to fight in the Tournament of Power. Universe 6 is also full of powerful warriors who were willing to do anything within their power to win the tournament and save their universe. Since it's parallel to Universe 7, it also has Saiyans with similar powers. During the final stretch of the tournament, Kale and Caulifa fused together and fought against Goku . Usually a fusion like that would ensure their victory, but even they never anticipated that Goku's Ultra Instinct state is on a league of its own.

Kefla used all her power to ensure Goku stays down, even to the point of exhausting her last bit of energy to launch powerful energy waves. Thanks to his Ultra Instinct state, Goku swiftly dodged each one of those attacks effortlessly, which otherwise would've been impossible. Instead of firing straight ahead, which he usually did , this time Goku rode along Kefla's giant energy wave to close the distance and get above her. Jumping through the energy waves, he managed to launch a Kamehameha that ensured his victory against Kefla with a point-blank finisher.

What truly makes this attack special is that this is the first time he used Kamehameha in his Ultra Instinct state, and it didn't fail in depicting the level of power Goku has been able to accomplish. It was already a fan-favorite moment among manga fans, but Toei Animation did justice to this scene with exceptional animation and fluid choreography, making it one of the best moments in Dragon Ball history.

Which Kamehameha moment in Dragon Ball Super is your personal favorite? Do you think any future battle could top Goku’s Kamehameha in Episode 116? Share your picks in the comments below.
