Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google In Marvel Comics' "Secret Wars," Doctor Doom recovered the pieces of a dead multiverse and then created something new out of the scraps. He built his own patchwork planet called Battleworld and filled it with remnants from all the destroyed Earths. This meant that the entire planet was split into different domains, each representing something that he was able to recover from the devastation of the incursions. He brought in the heroes and villains from those worlds and ensured they remembered nothing before their arrival in his new dystopian world. This made Battleworld more eclectic and diverse than anything Marvel Comics has ever seen.

While Doctor Doom and his family lived in his home of Doomstadt, repurposed for Battleworld, the rest of the planet featured everything from Ultron bots to Asgardians to the best characters to appear in the MCU's What If…? animated series, the Marvel Zombies.

Doomstadt is the capital of Battleworld, where God Emperor Doom and Sheriff Strange are based . Its locations include Castle Doom, the courts, and the Killiseum, a gladiatorial arena run by Arcade. Doom does not rule there alone. He reigns with his wife, Susan von Doom, and their children, Franklin and Valeria. One of the most interesting things there is Franklin's pet, Galactus. This is also where Battleworld's true strength lies, as the real Molecule Man, the being holding the entire world together, lives in an area beneath a statue of himself.

This is where most of Avengers: Secret Wars is likely to take place because this is where Doctor Doom lives, and it is where he rules over the entire world he created. It is also where the final battle happens. In the comics, Reed Richards faces off with Doom in the Molecule Man's base. This is also the safest place on Battleworld, thanks to the protection of Doctor Doom, and when people are exiled, that is when we discover all the other realms on the planet.

The Regency is an interesting realm on Battleworld, and it was made from what remained of Earth-18119. Its baron is Augustus Roman, the villain known as Regent, and this is where we can see Spider-Man in his biggest story from "Secret Wars." The realm was the setting of The Amazing Spider-Man: Renew Your Vows , a five-issue "Secret Wars" tie-in by Dan Slott and Adam Kubert. The Regency is a drastically reimagined incarnation of New York City.

Marvel called this "The Last Spider-Man Story." It brings back Peter Parker's wife and child, who had been removed from his continuity. Roman, the CEO of Empire Unlimited, killed the Avengers and the remaining heroes. He took their powers by harvesting genetic material from their bodies. Regent's rule is a police state for anyone with powers. His forces hunt down powered people, including children, and he sends the Sinister Six after Spider-Man. This could work in Avengers: Secret Wars by showing what would have happened if MJ had never forgotten her relationship with Peter Parker .

The Wastelands, the desert domain with Old Man Logan, is the Battleworld realm built from the remnants of Earth-21923, a variant of Earth-807128. This area includes Amerika, Hammer Falls, and New Vegas. Its tie-in is Old Man Logan #1 (2015) by Brian Michael Bendis and Andrea Sorrentino. It is set in a dystopia where villains rule because the heroes were killed, the same as the original "Old Man Logan" storyline from Wolverine comics. Just as in that world, Wolverine slaughtered the X-Men thanks to Mysterio's illusions.

In that original storyline, Logan killed the Hulk Gang and spared one baby, Bruce Banner Jr., to raise. This story opens with Logan breaking up a human trafficking ring and finding an Ultron Sentinel head. The head leads him to Hammer Falls and a dying Emma Frost, and because it came from beyond the Wastelands, he starts crossing borders. We have seen a version of Old Man Logan in Logan , and this could be a great place to bring the world back. Since that Wolverine died, this could bring back X-23 instead and show her in action in this world.

On Battleworld, Doctor Doom's law enforcement was the Thor Corps, and Doomgard is Doctor Doom's Asgard, which is where this police force operates from. Anyone from any domain who can lift a Mjolnir can join. This could bring in so many great characters to Avengers: Secret Wars, from Thor and Jane Foster to alternate versions of Thor and even Beta Ray Bill, who has yet to make his MCU debut. This realm debuted in Thors #1 (2015) by Jason Aaron and Chris Sprouse, and it was a police procedural series.

The murder victims are all versions of Jane Foster from different realities, each missing her eyes. Looking into any version of Jane Foster's eyes stirs any Thor's memory that something is wrong with the world. While the murder mystery would be too much for inclusion in a movie as big as Avengers: Secret Wars , seeing Doomgard would be incredible, and it could play a large role in how Doom keeps order on Battleworld.

The one Battleworld realm that has to be shown in Avengers: Secret Wars is the Deadlands. This is where anyone who is banished from Doomstadt is sent, and it is where the most popular What If…? characters from the animated series live. This is where the Marvel Zombies are found . The Deadlands is the Battleworld domain built from the remnants of the Marvel Zombies reality. It is infested with zombie versions of Marvel characters and lies outside God Emperor Doom's jurisdiction.

This realm brought in so many characters, from Captain Britain (Baron James Braddock), who was banished from Doomstadt, to Elsa Bloodstone, who is the main hero in the Marvel Zombies "Secret Wars" tie-in series. Late in "Secret Wars," Black Panther uses his title of King of the Dead to recruit the zombies against Doom, and there was even a series that showed the Marvel Zombies battling Ultron bots. There are so many great things about the Deadlands that if it doesn't show up in Avengers: Secret Wars , it would be a huge loss.

What Battleworld realms do you want to see in Avengers: Secret Wars ? Let us know what you want to see in the comments below.

articles.title: Trump’s $15 Billion Defamation Suit Against The New York Times Moves Forward
articles.summary: The court allowed seven allegedly defamatory statements to proceed while dismissing 27 others.
articles.content:
A federal judge has allowed portions of a defamation lawsuit from President Trump against The New York Times and four of its reporters accusing them of undermining his candidacy ahead of the 2024 presidential election to proceed.

U.S. District Judge Steven Merryday found on Thursday that the publication could've acted recklessly by advancing allegations linking Trump to tax crimes that were potentially "based on incomplete, minimal information."

Still, the court dismissed 27 statements Trump said were defamatory. It allowed seven others to move forward. They revolve around allegations in the book Lucky Loser and another Times story that Trump had received roughly $400 million from his father, much of it through tax evasion schemes, and that he was found to have violated money laundering rules, among other things.

In the ruling, Merryday concluded that a proper assessment of the Trump family's compliance with tax laws required forensic auditing and expert legal advice.

"The facts alleged in the complaint create at least a plausible inference that the authors and the publishers knew that no reliable conclusion about violations of the tax laws, including especially the estate and gift tax laws, is possible without reliance on qualified opinion formulated after the necessary factual and legal research and analysis, which they knowingly failed to obtain," the Republican-appointed judge wrote.

The ruling turned on an analysis of "actual malice," the legal standard in defamation cases involving public officials that requires a showing that the defendants knew the statements were false or acted with reckless disregard for the truth.

The Times argued that its reporters analyzed over 100,000 pages of financial records and consulted several experts, including tax specialists.

The court, however, said that analysis of tax and money laundering crimes is "intensely fact dependent" and that "only a relatively small cohort of specialized practitioners" are qualified to speak on such topics. Since the reporters failed to secure an explicit opinion from a qualified source that Trump had committed a crime, they had "particularized reason to doubt the truth of their statements."

Merryday said the Times ' reporting may constitute a "purposeful avoidance of the truth."

The four Times journalists named in the lawsuit are investigative reporters Susanne Craig and Russ Buettner, who wrote the book Lucky Loser: How Donald Trump Squandered His Father’s Fortune and Created the Illusion of Success , as well as Washington D.C. correspondent Michael S. Schmidt and White House correspondent Peter Baker.

The lawsuit seeks at least $15 billion and brings claims for defamation. It was filed by Alejandro Brito, who’s handled other media lawsuits for Trump.

articles.content:
We know Robert Pattinson is on Christopher Nolan ’s “nice list” considering he’s cast the actor in two of his movies. (Did you know Pattinson even helped inspire Nolan to make Oppenheimer ?) While the pair seem to have a great filmmaking partnership going, there was one time on the set of The Odyssey where Nolan totally rejected one choice Pattinson was hoping for on the spot.

Pattinson, of course, plays the very deplorable Antinous in The Odyssey . Before cameras started rolling, the actor reached out to the hair department to request a long wig for the part. As the movie’s hair department head Gloria Casny told it, when he called she just happened to be standing right next to Nolan. In her words:

That’s right. No conversation or negotiations, just “no”. Casny told the story during a news conference for The Odyssey in promotion of it becoming one of the latest 2026 movies that’s available to watch at home. The story led Matt Damon , who was the event’s moderator, to make this comment:

I can definitely see Pattinson’s vision for Antinous, but apparently one of Nolan’s rules is he doesn’t like to have actors wear any wigs or fake facial hair. Makes sense for the filmmaker who famously tries to do as much of his movies practically as possible.

Pattinson wasn’t the only actor on the set of The Odyssey that made a request to the hair department. As Matt Damon told USA Today during the same event, he had actually asked Nolan if he could have a fake beard to play Odysseus. Can you guess Nolan’s answer? Per Damon’s words:

Same reaction! How funny. Damon really did grow a magnificent beard though, so it all worked out. And, honestly Pattinson’s forward-swept bangs fit perfectly, too. You can appreciate the lack of wigs on The Odyssey by purchasing it for home viewing now.

articles.title: Major Fantasy Reboot Confirms Season 2 Return After 3 Years With New Look
articles.summary: Rebooted adaptations of classic anime franchises have become increasingly popular in recent years, with seasonal lineups featuring star-studded titles making massive comebacks like Science Saru's modernized spin on Ghost in the Shell and TMS Entertainment's reboot of Fruits Basket, both of which promised to deliver stories that were more faithful retellings of their respective source […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Rebooted adaptations of classic anime franchises have become increasingly popular in recent years, with seasonal lineups featuring star-studded titles making massive comebacks like Science Saru's modernized spin on Ghost in the Shell and TMS Entertainment's reboot of Fruits Basket , both of which promised to deliver stories that were more faithful retellings of their respective source materials. This trend is only set to continue with the long-awaited announcement that Studio Passione's reboot of Isuna Hakekura's original series Spice and Wolf will be getting a second season. The series has joined the Winter 2027 Anime Season with a release window set for sometime in January.

The first season of the Spice and Wolf reboot promised a more faithful adaptation of the original light novel from Isuna Hakekura compared to its 2008 predecessor from Imagin. In that, Season 1 adapted volumes 1 through 4 of the original series, including the fourth volume's Legend of the Pagan God's arc, which the original anime skipped, as well as tying in a short story featured in the series' seventh volume. The reboot was met with overwhelming praise from fans, and now the series will finally be making a return to continue the anime's adaptation of previously skipped story material, including Volume 6 of the original light novel series which has never been animated before.

Spice and Wolf focuses on the travels of Kraft Lawrence , a wandering merchant who, in a chance encounter, meets Holo: a harvest deity with wolf-like traits who joins him in his travels to return to her homeland. Along the way, the pair continue to manage Lawrence's mercantile business and navigate the politics of the land in their journey. While many fantasy series similar to Spice and Wolf take its heroes on some grand, "save the world" adventure, Holo and Kraft's story is more of a slow burn tale that puts emphasis on building the world they exist in and the many faces they encounter on their way north.

Spice and Wolf is famous for its slow burn romance between Holo and Kraft as well, showcasing the dichotomy of their lives as a spirt-human pair, and the stark differences in their ambitions. The series is a critical and commercial success as well, in 2020, just four years before the anime's reboot began releasing, the original light novel series had sold over 5 million copies, with the English localization of the series debuting at No. 4 on The New York Times Bestsellers List for manga. In the 2007 edition of Kono Light Novel ga Sugoi! , Holo ranked first in the "Best Female Category," a testament to how dedicated readers were to the wolf deity when the series was at its peak.

The original anime adaptation from Imagin in 2008, as well as its second season in 2009 from Brain's Base and Marvy Jack drew out the series already slow burn pacing with multiple anime-original filler arcs while skipping an entire volume's worth of material. This resulted in the second season of the original Spice and Wolf anime to end on a cliffhanger that took the reboot a single season to reach. Additionally, the original anime adaptation replaced one of the light novel's characters, a man named Yarei, with an anime-original female character named Chloe. This caused much of Lawrence and Holo's characterization to shift, as well as some of the thematic implications of their relationship.

In the novels and 2024 adaptation of the anime, Yarei is a young up-and-coming farmer with aspirations to become a merchant from Pasloe who serves as Lawrence's foil early in the story. While Yarei serves as something of an antagonist in these versions of the story, his replacement in the 2008 anime, Chloe, is also antagonistic — but for a completely different reason. Chloe is introduced as another aspiring merchant from Pasloe with similar ambitions to Yarei, however, Chloe's character differs greatly in that much of her conflict comes from her unrequited feelings for Lawrence.

While she shared similar struggles to Yarei, such as her dreams to modernize Pasloe and no longer rely on a pagan deity, the sudden injection that she and Holo be romantic rivals felt suffocating among the ongoing religious and economic conflict already present in the story. Considering how hard the the team at Studio Passione have worked to bring the complete, original story of Spice and Wolf to life , the second season releasing in 2027 should remain just as faithful as the first. What do you think of the Spice and Wolf reboot so far? Let us know in the comments.

Black Bear has acquired the North American rights to Bill Hader 's feature directorial debut " They Know ." Hader also wrote and stars in the horror-thriller with Linda Cardellini .

Based on an idea from Hader and his "Barry" collaborator Duffy Boudreau, "'They Know' follows a divorced dad who becomes increasingly suspicious and paranoid that his ex-wife's new mysterious partner is exerting a strange, unsettling influence on their children," according to an official logline. Hader serves as producer with Bob Graf under his Hanarply banner. Alyssa Donovan is co-producer. MRC fully financed the film, which is currently in post-production. The long awaited and twice delayed launch of Grand Theft Auto VI has made a killing and taken over the zeitgeist.

By killing, we don't just mean the mayhem of Vice City. We mean cold hard cash, digitally

Less than 24 hours after the fictional Florida-set video game went live at midnight today, GTA VI has made over $2.36 billion, according to Sensor Tower. In fact, with last night's fully GTA VI themed Miami Heat 's primetime 137-130 win over the Milwaukee Bucks as but one example of the vast marketing machine at play, sales surged in the final hours before launch as fans rushed to download the 212GB game. Cementing the latest Rockstar Games ' offering as the most successful entertainment industry launch ever, the decade and more in the making GTA VI saw sales rise $710 million since early on November 18 when pre-sales sat at an already record breaking $1.65 billion. Currently, the download only GTA VI has sold 24.59 million units, with 75% of them on Playstation and the remainder on Xbox consoles.

At this rate, with millions around the globe seemingly taking an adult snow day or PTO to play the first new GTA game in 13 years, VI is on track to reach further financial heights of $3 billion within weeks. That figure could be dwarfed when the single player GTA VI lands on the multi-player and lucrative GTA Online platform in the next several months.

As large as that number will go, leaving far far behind, the previous launch day number #1 of the $800 million GTA V earned in 2013, the (mis)adventures of crooks on the rise Jason and Lucia in the corrupt and free-wheeling humid state of Leonida is having an almost equal impact on the culture. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

A throwback in more ways than one to the long lost days of American monoculture, the eighth full game in the GTA franchise has conquered the conversation online and offline today.

Estimates of economic losses due to absentee workers Thursday may be offset by GTA VI profits, but nothing could stop a full partisan upbraiding from Fox News . “If this generation wants to preach about affordability, but they’re willing to cost billions of dollars in revenue loss on a day like today to go play a game, that probably tells you everything you need to know about what we need to be talking with this younger generation about," the Murdoch-owned cabler newser's Harris Faulkner declared this AM. "Get yourself to work."

Of course, taking into account the controversy that the ultra violent GTA franchise has courted since its 1997 debut, such a berating falls nicely into the best tradition of the P.T. Barnum's supposed quip of "there is no such thing as bad publicity." Along with Fox, CNN , NewsNation, the BBC , the New York Times, the Guardian and the upscale New Yorker have all run a number of segments and features on VI today. On YouTube and Twitch, hundreds of live feeds are up busting internet viewership with millions watching people playing the over 150 hour long game or detailing hacks, easter eggs and just cruising around.

To that, GTA VI has also been name dropped and appropriated today by an unlikely in any other circumstances collection of bandwagon jumpers.

The White House, HGTV , a sycophantic Vice-President JD Vance , Miami International Airport, Matt Johnson's The The (who legitimately has a tune once again on one of the many in-game radio stations), Spotify , the Interior Department, and the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, have all been hooking themselves to GTA VI in some witty, some cringe inducing and some just meh posts.

To paraphrase that big Hot Chocolate hit, everyone loves a winner, baby.

articles.title: Where to Find GTA 6’s X-Men Parody Comic & How The Characters Compare
articles.summary: GTA 6 is finally here and as fans dig into the long-awaited game, there is a lot to explore and discover. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google GTA 6 is finally here and as fans dig into the long-awaited game, there is a lot to explore and discover. People are discovering that some “iconic” features from past games, but are finding plenty of new features, challenges, and even some surprises — including a hilarious X-Men parody that pretty much no one would have expected that is not only funny, but honestly kind of holds up.

As users have shared on line, there are more than 30 various magazines and comic books located in GTA 6 , including the RX-Men comic book. The comic, published by the in-world fictional ED Comics, is priced at $1.25 and is available for purchase at the 24/7 store in Key Lento. But while the in-game book is an interesting bit of fun-poking at real world elements like the popularity of superheroes and the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday , what’s especially interesting about RX-Men is how it satirizes the iconic heroes and turns them into a much bigger joke.

A ‘X-MEN’ parody exists within GTA 6. (📸: @dzakidj ) pic.twitter.com/ziWH31W2hW

While most Marvel Comics fans are familiar with the Merry Mutants and their wide range of powers and sometimes unique physical appearances thanks to decades of comics as well as movies, GTA 6 twists the idea into a pharmaceutical satire.  The cover features a very Magneto-esque figure named Dr. Placebo who the book reveals “seeks to free the world of pharmaceuticals” with his “army of alt medicine minions”. There are also the heroes with Capsule, Side Effect, Diagnosis, and Mr. I, the latter of which is a play on MRI.

The satire here is what’s fascinating. The RX-Men appear to represent, essentially, better living through chemistry or in this case, medication and medical care while Dr. Placebo represents people who think those things are a scam at best and toxic at worst — there’s an image where a devotee of Dr. Placebo tells his worried partner who tells him to take his medication or he’ll die to shut up and give him raw milk instead while another devotee has just one month to live and is trusting Dr. Placebo’s crystals rather than medical care. It’s a clear bit of satire about the alternative healthcare movement, but that also doesn’t mean the RX-Men are free of satirization. Side Effect — which appears to be a satire of Beast — has a laundry list of serious medical conditions that makes him pretty much useless leading to the RX-Men’s Jean Grey, Diagnosis to step in instead.

Of course, RX-Men isn’t the only book you can find in the GTA 6 world of comics. Another ED Comic you can find in the game is Ratface, which is very clearly a parody of DC Comics’ Batman. Of course, here, RX-Men and Ratface are from the same publisher so who knows, maybe GTA 6 has the Marvel/DC crossover we crave.

GTA 6 is out now. Have you found the RX-Men comic in game? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
Are two directors better than one?

Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, Phil Lord and Chris Miller and Nigeria’s Esiri brothers are chasing a prize the Academy’s Director Branch has handed to a duo only three times in its history.

Looking at the two-name directing teams in this year’s Oscar race, artistic collaboration seems to be having a moment. Not everyone sees it that way. Related Stories Netflix Alum Emily Feingold Joins Disney as Executive VP of Communications Gang Dong-won, Kim Go-eun to Star in Netflix’s 'The Twilight Between Us' From 'When Life Gives You Tangerines' Director, 'Queen of Tears' Writer

“If you need two of you to make the film, then I think that’s a problem,” one prominent member of the Directors Branch bluntly tells Variety. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Fielder and Oppenheim turned Elizabeth Holmes’ saga into the slippery A24 documentary “ You Can See Everything .” Calvo and Ambrossi, the Spanish duo known as Los Javis, are carrying their country’s international feature hopes with “ La Bola Negra .” Lord and Miller reunited behind the camera for Amazon MGM’s sci-fi swing “Project Hail Mary.” And twin brothers Arie and Chuko Esiri helmed Neon’s ambitious “Clarissa,” a reimagining of “Mrs. Dalloway.”

All four teams face a stubborn piece of Academy history: The Directors Branch does not like splitting statuettes. In 98 years, only four directing duos have received best director nominations (one of them twice). This year, several are within earshot of nods.

Robert Wise and Jerome Robbins got there first for 1961’s “West Side Story.” Their partnership was so combustible that Robbins was fired mid-production for running over schedule and budget. He retained his credit and collected the Oscar.

Warren Beatty and Buck Henry followed with “Heaven Can Wait” (1978), but lost to Michael Cimino (“The Deer Hunter”). Joel and Ethan Coen scored for the best picture winner “No Country for Old Men” (2007), and were nominated again for the Western remake “True Grit” (2010), losing out to Tom Hooper (“The King’s Speech”). The most recent winners, Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert, aka the Daniels, took home the prize for “Everything Everywhere All at Once” (2022). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

History suggests that longtime professional partnerships are the key to acceptance. Wise and Robbins were a filmmaker and a choreographer brought together by a studio. The Daniels met making music videos. The Coens remain the only sibling duo recognized.

The Academy has repeatedly overlooked pairings, even in the face of precursor support. Jonathan Dayton and Valerie Faris, the married filmmakers behind “Little Miss Sunshine” (2006), won SAG ensemble and PGA honors and earned a DGA feature nom. The Oscars ’ directing branch still shut them out.

The Safdie brothers were similarly snubbed for “Uncut Gems” (2019), but when Josh Safdie made his solo debut with “Marty Supreme” last year, the branch gave him a nod. Even the Wachowskis couldn’t crack the category for the revolutionary technical achievement of “The Matrix” (1999).

This season’s teams fit familiar types. Lord and Miller and Fielder and Oppenheim resemble the Daniels’ professional partnership, while the Esiri siblings are following the Coens’ path. Los Javis are the wild card: The couple’s roughly 13-year romantic relationship ended while they were making “La Bola Negra,” their most personal and ambitious collaboration.

“The first question other directors will ask is ‘Why did you need two people to do this?’” one veteran strategist says. “The job is to convince a bunch of directors who often think they are the most creative artists alive that their genius can be shared. That’s tough.”

None of the four teams is a conventional frontrunner. Fielder and Oppenheim are competing in a documentary lane the Directors Branch has always kept separate. Los Javis are more likely to make noise in international feature and screenplay because theirs is a non-English-language film. Lord and Miller are the closest thing to a studio-scale contender, but genre films need to overperform in below-the-line races to enter the conversation.

Still, the sheer number of teams is the story. Four duos in one year reflects an industry increasingly built on shared creative enterprise, even as many directors cling to the myth of the solo genius.

articles.title: Love Overgeared? Watch These 3 Anime Next
articles.summary: Overgeared has emerged as the biggest webtoon anime adaptation of the Fall 2026 season, gaining recognition as a Solo Leveling replacement as well. However, the anime is more than just a replacement for Solo Leveling with similar elements, as it has its own nuances that set it apart from other webtoons that have received anime […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Overgeared has emerged as the biggest webtoon anime adaptation of the Fall 2026 season, gaining recognition as a Solo Leveling replacement as well. However, the anime is more than just a replacement for Solo Leveling with similar elements, as it has its own nuances that set it apart from other webtoons that have received anime adaptations.

It achieves this through a very different protagonist, featuring a laid-back hero who is desperate for power and wealth, something constantly highlighted through his actions. Meanwhile, it also incorporates game and leveling-up systems, elements that have become increasingly popular in the anime industry. This is why there are several anime similar to Overgeared , two of which were released this year, including one that is currently airing.

One of the intriguing elements of Overgeared is undoubtedly its power fantasy, as Grid continues to grow stronger with every new obstacle. However, what sets it apart is its incorporation of comedy through its protagonist and the elements that complement his character. This is exactly why the currently airing anime The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life is a great choice for Overgeared fans to watch alongside it in Fall 2026. The series features a laid-back protagonist, Rein, who gets kicked out of his party because he is no longer needed.

Since Rein was an enhancer and his party members had already maxed out their weapons, he was dismissed. As he leaves, he takes back all the enhancements he had provided to his party members and transfers them into a copper sword. This turns his weapon into an overpowered asset capable of withstanding anything that comes his way. Its laid-back journey, hilarious moments, and Rein's crafting skills make this anime remarkably similar to Overgeared , allowing it to scratch that same itch better than almost any other series.

Another anime that aired this year and is fairly similar to Overgeared is Tomb Raider King . The anime was dubbed a replacement for Solo Leveling in Summer 2026 , and with Overgeared being labeled the replacement for Solo Leveling in Fall, fans are sure to enjoy either series if they liked the other. Tomb Raider King also features a protagonist on a journey of self-development, but it adds the intrigue of time travel to the mix.

Having regressed in time, Seo Jooheon takes his second chance seriously, acquiring everything he needs for his self-development. What makes this refreshing is its older protagonist, making his choices and journey feel more mature and serious rather than comedic. Jooheon's actions are also quite brutal, allowing him to overshadow even Solo Leveling 's Jinwoo in this regard. With a unique leveling-up system that further incorporates the gaming theme, Tomb Raider King is a must-watch for fans of both Solo Leveling and Overgeared .

With virtual reality gaming serving as its foundation, Overgeared is an MMORPG built around the game Satisfy. This is why Shangri-La Frontier is arguably the anime that comes closest to what Overgeared represents. It features a protagonist who has played numerous trash games before moving on to the popular virtual reality game Shangri-La Frontier and embarking on a quest to dominate it. Going by the in-game name Sunraku and sporting a bird mask, the series makes comedy one of its biggest strengths.

Sunraku is always in tactical mode, finding the best possible ways to acquire loot and rewards. The series delivers pretty much everything expected of a game-based narrative, exploring new areas, fighting new bosses, and gearing up, while other online players also make their presence felt throughout the story. If what Overgeared has offered so far appeals to you, then there is arguably no better anime than Shangri-La Frontier to scratch that same itch.

articles.title: What Is Snoggletog? All The Tea On The Celebration At Universal Orlando This Holiday Season
articles.summary: It’s beginning to look a lot like Snoggletog in the Isle of Berk.
articles.content:
The love, joy and merriment of the holiday season are always infectious in theme parks. As part of Universal Epic Universe’s holiday celebration expansion for 2026, the decorations have been scaled up (sorry, I had to work a dragon reference in there) in How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk for Snoggletog, and guests are all the better for it.

For those not in the know, Snoggletog is the winter holiday celebrated by the Viking community on the fictional Isle of Berk in the How to Train Your Dragon franchise. It features feasts and festivities fit for dragons and even includes the seasonal Harvest Mac & Cheese Cone at Hooligan’s Grog & Gruel. And there’s now a row of trees, just inside the entrance, decorated with what looks to be homemade ornaments that are a fun detail to check out during the day and beautiful to look at once they’re lit up at night.

I have to say, the thing that most caught my eye was the wreath full of apples. It’s the perfect decor idea that not only looks beautifully festive but would also just be delicious. I also love that you can find a tree made of wood inside Hiccup’s Workshop that you could probably easily replicate if you’re crafty, or you can just pick up themed ornaments for your own home holiday tree.

So, with that in mind, it's always fun to see how people react to being the subject of a question featured on the show. Case in point: Ice-T had a very funny take when he found out that someone didn't know he was the answer to Final Jeopardy! .

Final Jeopardy! can literally make or break someone’s future on the long-running game show. The clues can range from history to literature to, yes, even pop culture. On the episode from the 2026 TV schedule that aired on October 28 , Ice-T was the answer for the final round. Two people got it right, but one person was wrong. Ice-T addressed the moment while appearing on the Today Show and revealed just what he thinks of the whole ordeal:

I’m in a lot of crossword puzzles, because Ice-T, I-C-E-T, is a weird spelled thing. But Jeopardy, I’ve been in Jeopardy before, but Final Jeopardy. …. [They asked] who put out an album, Home Invasion, and also is the longest-running character in television. And the guy said Tim Allen. I think he was thinking about Home Improvement, right? But the two women got it right, and I only care about the women [laughs]. So, you know, he lost, and they won. But that’s how it goes. But Final Jeopardy!’s a big deal.

Of course, being a clue on Jeopardy! is a big deal, even if it does sting when someone does not know the answer. And as Ice-T pointed out, he’s been in plenty of clues over the years. That being said, it’s a lot different when you’re in Final Jeopardy!

Overall, I love that Ice-T wasn’t too hurt over being mistaken for Tim Allen , and instead focused on the fact that the two women got it right, which is all he cares about. I'm also very entertained by the image of Tim Allen trying to rap.

Anyway, the clue was for the category “Current TV Streaks,” and it just shows that even if a clue seems easy, it may not be for a lot of people. For host Ken Jennings , there was one category that made him nervous when he was competing, and it was surprisingly hockey. While he wound up being one of the biggest Jeopardy! winners of all time and no one has yet to beat his 74-game streak, it sounds like that still haunts him. So, everyone has their blind spots.

Despite the fact that Law & Order: SVU is in its 28 th season, it’s wild to me that Ice-T has been playing Odafin “Fin” Tutuola for almost three decades. He’s been on the NBC drama since the second season and is one of the longest-running actors in the Law & Order franchise . Luckily, he doesn’t have any plans to leave any time soon. While he has been worried that he’d be written out as the show has had to make room for Kellie Giddish , that has not been the case.

Hopefully, the next time Ice-T is an answer for Final Jeopardy! everyone gets it right. However, even if it’s just the women, I’m sure he will be just fine. articles.title: 5 Game of Thrones Characters Totally Ruined by the HBO TV Series
articles.summary: There's no denying that Game of Thrones is one of the greatest shows in television history. There's also no denying that the series ultimately failed many of its major characters and storylines with its widely panned final season. Jon Snow's clearly important parentage played no part in those last few episodes, Daenerys Targaryen's turn to […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There's no denying that Game of Thrones is one of the greatest shows in television history. There's also no denying that the series ultimately failed many of its major characters and storylines with its widely panned final season. Jon Snow's clearly important parentage played no part in those last few episodes, Daenerys Targaryen's turn to "mad queen" felt rushed, Jaime Lannister's arc was totally tossed aside, and the villainous Cersei Lannister got one of the most unsatisfying endings ever. That said, most of the time we spent with those characters on the show was great, intriguing, and felt true to who they were in the books.

While you could write pages about those characters, they were hurt by the fact that the books aren't finished. We're discussing the characters who were more interesting in the A Song of Ice and Fire novels, yet the adaptations brought to Game of Thrones on the small screen reduced them to one or two smaller aspects and resulted in disappointing versions. In some cases, they were good but better in the books, while in other situations, the show turned them into hollow shells of what they could have been.

Stannis Baratheon is incredibly unlikable in both the show and the novels, yet the books make sure he's a bit more nuanced. He's driven by his duty and the fact that he understands the Iron Throne to be his by birthright, rather than because he's greedy and wants it. The show has him be complicit in Melisandre's killing of his brother Renly and he often comes across as a religious zealot for the Lord of Light (though not quite as much as his wife is).

The novels use his belief in Melisandre alongside his own beliefs in his duties, which play against each other. It makes for intriguing chapters, especially through the eyes of POV character Davos. It's unclear if Stannis would actually burn his daughter alive in the books, but if he did, it would likely be better fleshed out than due to bad weather ahead of a battle. Stannis will never be anyone's favorite character, but he's a pivotal piece of the story and works well as a cautionary tale for others vying for the throne, so the show turning him into someone far less interesting is disappointing.

Varys is one of those characters who is good in the show, yet when you read about him, you gain a whole new appreciation for him. The Master of Whisperers was always a step ahead of everyone outside of maybe Littlefinger. While that is depicted well on the screen, the Varys of the books is something else entirely. For starters, we never get to see how he's a master of disguise. In the novels, Varys takes on many forms and can change the way he speaks so he's unrecognizable. Even Tyrion takes a while to realize who he's talking to at one point.

Varys is also more of a Targaryen loyalist in the books (some theories even say Varys is actually a Targaryen ) and is even rumored to be behind the plot that allows Young Griff, Rhaegar's actual son, to escape King's Landing as a baby. The Young Griff subplot is one of the biggest mysteries left in the novels. As the show went on and avoided that story, Varys became less cunning and far less interesting.

This may be a controversial pick because Robb Stark feels more prominent in the show. In the novels, he and Rickon are the only Starks who aren't POV characters, so Robb's story is seen through the eyes of Catelyn. In Game of Thrones , we watch plenty of scenes from his rise as the King in the North to his untimely death at the Red Wedding. However, the show made a major change that made Robb worse as a character.

In the books, Robb is comforted by Jeyne Westerling after learning of his brothers' supposed deaths. They sleep together and Robb marries her to protect her honor, while in the show, Robb simply falls for Talisa and throws everything away to marry her. This takes away from a key aspect of Robb's story, which is how his downfall mirrors that of Ned Stark. He's so much like his father that his honor and honesty lead him to marry Jeyne instead of the Frey he was promised to, resulting in the Red Wedding. Without that honor aspect, Robb is just someone who made a bad decision with his heart, which is far less intriguing.

A Feast for Crows is often seen as the worst book in A Song of Ice and Fire , yet it does shine a light on the Martells and the Grejoys. That means a lot of time is given to Euron Greyjoy, who is one of the scariest characters in the franchise. He's someone who is incredibly ambitious while also being increasingly dangerous. He basically wants to become a god, steal a dragon, and is willing to dabble in the dark arts to get what he wants.

Euron's standing heading into The Winds of Winter is one of the most interesting elements of the series. He could change the face of Westeros and the battle for the Iron Throne entirely. Unfortunately, Game of Thrones changed him into a generic, campy villain. The TV show counterpart doesn't seem nearly as threatening and his ambition often comes down to wanting to have sex with the Queen. Nothing captivating about Euron remained and what we got was a hollow shell of someone who could've changed the game in the final seasons.

It might be kind of a cop-out to group all of Dorne together but Game of Thrones messed them all up so badly that it's hard not to. In the books, Doran Martell is a cunning man who is playing the long game in his desire for revenge against the Lannisters, to the point where almost nobody knows what he's planning. The strategic elements of his story are some of the highlights of the last few books. The show just plays on the idea that he's weak, which he's mostly feigning in the novels, and doesn't do anything beyond that, making him a passive character.

The Sand Snakes are ruined in the show by becoming interchangable. They give no time to differentiate Oberyn's daughters, so nobody cares about them. In the books, each has their own nuanced personality, are diverse, and each is carrying out a plot from Doran , adding so much to the Dorne storylines. The show also entirely cut Doran's heir Ariane Martell, who had her own great plans, and basically melded some of those ideas into Ellaria and the Sand Snakes. What should've been a gripping political subplot was reduced to nothing of interest and viewers often groaned when a Dorne scene came on TV, which isn't how it should've been.

Which A Song of Ice and Fire character do you think Game of Thrones messed up the most? Let us know in the comments.

Playbill is apologizing for running an ad for singers for a cast album called "George Floyd the Musical" from the Busted Broadway company.

The project drew numerous negative comments from Broadway stars and many others. Busted Broadway responded on its social media Thursday that "The project 'George Floyd the Musical' is NOT making light of, condoning, or mocking the horrific 2020 murder of George Floyd. It’s a satire on the CULTURE, rather than the person. Never judge a show by its title, as many who have never seen the script or score appear to be doing now.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘Gordon,’ a Big Netflix Series From Argentina, Unpacked by Pablo Trapero and Star Rodrigo de la Serna 'Stranger Things' Prequel Spinoff 'Other Worlds' Ordered to Series at Netflix

We at Playbill aim to lift up this community with empathy, consideration, and respect. We hope those who read and follow us do the same.

"We know this listing has upset and offended many, and the fact that it made it onto our site has disappointed those who trust us as an outlet," the post continued.

articles.title: Dragon Ball Super Already Locked In the Next Z Fighter & They Need Their Anime Debut
articles.summary: Almost every Dragon Ball arc adds another warrior to the Z Fighters, and Granolah looks like he could be next. The last remaining Cerealian boasts all the key characteristics that fit into Goku's band of highly moral misfits. Granolah survived the destruction of his planet thanks to Bardock, but it doesn't come without collateral damage. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Almost every Dragon Ball arc adds another warrior to the Z Fighters, and Granolah looks like he could be next. The last remaining Cerealian boasts all the key characteristics that fit into Goku's band of highly moral misfits. Granolah survived the destruction of his planet thanks to Bardock, but it doesn't come without collateral damage. The situation creates Granolah's deep disdain toward the Saiyans, by proxy of Frieza. He doesn't care where the sole blame lays at the start of his arc, but he eventually understands that the evil emperor is to blame. The manga introduced him some time ago, but he awaits his anime debut .

Granolah also didn't join up with the Z Fighters after his arc was completed. Goku and Vegeta offered him up the opportunity to come train with them. However, he decides to stay and gather the Dragon Balls. He currently continues his journey and hasn't made an appearance since in the manga. The way Granolah's story ends is incomplete, so there's no way he won't get an expanded role later .

Similar to Tien, Piccolo and Vegeta, these former foes turned allies realize what a good person Goku is and what he's trying to accomplish. Vegeta in particular looks to just avenge his planet, similar to Granolah, but goes the wrong way about it initially. His change to the Z Fighters took some more time, but Granolah ran through similar problems. He's never told about Bardock protecting him . He's just told the Saiyans caused his race's destruction.

Granolah works for the Heeters, who use his disdain for the Saiyans, to try and defeat Goku and Vegeta. The plan backfires, as Granolah discovers the truth and flips sides. Even though he's not a Saiyan or Namekian, Granolah has proven himself to be a competent fighter and representative of his race. Cerealians use an enhanced right eye to find their opponents' weak points, and he regularly proves he can do so in his battles with Goku and Vegeta.

A way to get Granolah and Frieza's recent new transformation, Black Frieza , into the anime, is that the two eventually duke it out. With Granolah's recent power-up wish, there isn't much time. The Cerealian gave up 150 years of his life to attain all the power levels he would've achieved in his life right away. The choice gives him a limited amount of time to find Frieza and defeat him.

Worlds are set to collide with Frieza's return in the arc and Granolah's hunt for him. In fact, at the time that the Frieza Force was around for the Cerealian destruction, King Cold and a non-canon Cooler would have been alive. This would be a great opportunity to bring the Frieza family back into the story and give them the proper, revenge-filled defeat at the hands of the last living Cerealian.

Granolah is canon, so it's not like bringing him into the fold would be that difficult. No retconning required, just an easy addition is all that needs to happen. Granolah would add another great fighter capable of going toe-to-toe with high-powered enemies and also a new ability that can aid the group. His long range attacks and quick-study of rival fighters could certainly come in handy. Should Granolah be brought into Dragon Ball Super 's anime future? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Cast Guide: All the Tributes, Mentors and Younger Versions of Characters in Prequel
articles.summary: Before Katniss Everdeen ever volunteered as tribute for the Hunger Games, another District 12 victor made his way out of the arena, but with much fewer odds in his favor. “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is set 24 years before the first “Hunger Games” film (and 40 years after “The Ballad of Songbird […]
articles.content:
Joseph Zada stars as Haymitch Abernathy, a tribute from District 12 who is the future mentor to the main series’ protagonist, Katniss Everdeen. Despite being born on the same day as the Reaping, Haymitch’s birthday luck runs short when he is selected for the second Quarter Quell and soon finds himself on President Snow's radar after publicly defying the capitol.

Throughout the film, Haymitch is thrust into several intense moments, whether they are grounded in emotion or consist of demanding action sequences. One of Zada’s favorite scenes is a particular battle near the end of the film, which he tells Variety makes him “look like a fucking action star.”

“In terms of acting, I just want to throw myself completely in the deep end with every project. And it helps so much having that attitude in the arena, because that’s just my character the whole time,” Zada says. “He’s really going for it, and I was like, ‘There’s no way for me to do this believably unless I’m throwing myself down that mountain or pushing myself to the edge of death and almost injuring myself every single day. There was no other way for me to do that and make it believable without just completely diving in the deep end.”

Haymitch Abernathy was played by Woody Harrelson in the original films.

Joining Haymitch in the second Quarter Quell is District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner, who's played by Mckenna Grace and is the original owner of Katniss’ mockingjay pin. Initially at odds with her fellow District 12 tributes, Maysilee eventually joins their alliance with the Newcomers and grows particularly close to Haymitch, encouraging him to defy the Capitol.

As a long-time fan of the “Hunger Games” franchise, Grace tells Variety she wanted her portrayal of Maysilee to be accurate to Collins’ source material. One of the things she prioritized was keeping the character’s anger consistent throughout the film instead of having her arc of “learning to be kinder diminish her anger.

“While she finds happiness in being kind to the people around her and protecting them, she's still a very angry character. And I think that it's really important to show young women and anyone in general that the two can coexist,” she says. “You can be very angry at the world, or you can be very loud about the things that you believe in and in standing up for yourself and the people around you. But you can also be kind throughout that.

Grace also portrays Merilee Donner, Maysilee’s twin sister. Her previous credits include “I, Tonya,” “Regretting You,” “The Handmaid’s Tale” and “Ghostbusters: Afterlife.” She is next set to star in “Scooby Doo: Origins” as a young Daphne Blake.

Lenore Dove Baird is Haymitch’s girlfriend and a descendant of the Covey, which Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zelger) was a part of in "Songbirds and Snakes." After her mother died during childbirth, Lenore Dove was raised by her uncles Tam Amber and Clerk Carmine Clade, whom audiences met in the previous prequel. Whitney Peak plays the character after starring in films like “Molly’s Game” and series such as “Chilling Adventures of Sabrina.”

Ralph Fiennes stars as Coriolanus Snow, the cruel and tyrannical president of Panem who previously mentored Lucy Gray Baird, a District 12 tribute who won the 10th Hunger Games. After Haymitch publicly defies the Capitol, Snow marks him as a target and stops at nothing to suppress his resistance. No stranger to playing the villain, Fiennes has also starred as the antagonist in “The Menu” and as Voldemort in the “Harry Potter” franchise. Snow was played by Donald Sutherland in the original films and by Tom Blyth in “The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes.”

Elle Fanning plays Effie Trinket, a Capitol stylist who steps in to help dress the District 12 tributes for their interviews. Effie ultimately becomes the district’s escort in the original films, where she was played by Elizabeth Banks. Earlier this year, Fanning received an Emmy nomination for “Margo’s Got Money Troubles” after previously starring in “A Complete Unknown,” “Maleficent” and “Super 8.”

Plutarch Heavensbee is a cameraman assigned to cover District 12 during the Hunger Games. Although he serves as a trusted advisor to President Snow, Plutarch is secretly involved in the growing rebellion against the Capitol and helps Haymitch execute his plan to break the arena. He’s played by Jesse Plemons, who also starred in “Bugonia,” “The Power of the Dog,” “Kinds of Kindness” and “Game Night.” Plutarch ultimately becomes a gamemaker for the third Quarter Quell in “Catching Fire,” where he is played by Philip Seymour Hoffman for the remainder of the original films.

As the host of the Hunger Games, Caesar Flickerman is responsible for keeping Capitol citizens entertained and invested throughout the annual event. Typically known for his bold outfits and quick-witted humor, the role was originated by Stanley Tucci and is now played by Kieran Culkin, whose previous credits include “Succession” and “A Real Pain.” Caesar's grandfather Lucky (Jason Schwartzman) was the announcer in "Songbirds and Snakes."

Drusilla Sickle is a Capitol chaperone for the District 12 tributes. Openly disdainful of the poor district, particularly Maysilee, Drusilla hopes to earn a promotion to a higher-ranking group of tributes and takes extreme measures to ensure her presentations are nothing short of perfection. Glenn Close stars as the vain escort after playing a similarly eccentric character in “101 Dalmatians.” She is also known for her roles in “Fatal Attraction” and “Dangerous Liaisons.”

Billy Porter plays Magno Stift, a reptile-loving Capitol stylist unwillingly assigned to the District 12 tributes. Magno puts little effort into dressing the tributes on the rare occasion he decides to show up. Porter is largely known for his stage career, having starred in Broadway shows including “Kinky Boots,” “Cabaret” and “Shuffle Along.”

After winning the 34th Hunger Games, Beetee secretly conspired against the Capitol, which President Snow eventually discovered. Now, Snow is punishing the District 3 victor by reaping his son, Ampert, for the second Quarter Quell. Kelvin Harrison Jr. plays the character after starring in films including “Mufasa: The Lion King" and “Elvis." Jeffrey Wright originated the role in the previous films.

Also a fan of the franchise, Harrison Jr. tells Variety that, while he would refer to the books and Wright's performance, he primarily focused on the world and character that the screenwriters of "Sunrise on the Reaping" created for that specific moment in time.

"What they [the screenwriters] gave me the real estate for was really fleshing out a sense of knowingness that there is no space for grief for him right now. He is in a position where there isn't self-preservation," Harrison Jr. says. "There is overcoming in order to have a larger cause to take care of a larger party, and what's at stake is his own flesh and blood. And I wanted to figure out how to navigate the feeling of grief as something you can't really control, but you're trying to outrun it. But you really can't."

Harrison Jr. and Wright previously played father and son in 2018's "Monster" and will do so again in "Samo Lives," the upcoming Jean-Michel Basquiat biopic.

Wiress is the exceptionally intelligent victor of the 49th Hunger Games who, alongside Mags, mentors Haymitch, Maysilee, Wyatt and Lou Lou for the second Quarter Quell. She is played by Maya Hawke, who is known for her roles in “Stranger Things,” “Do Revenge” and “Inside Out 2,” and was originated by Amanda Plummer in “The Hunger Games: Catching Fire.”

Little is known about Wiress beyond the fact that her arena was filled with mirrors and that she won without killing a single tribute. Hawke tells Variety she "relished in" every piece of information she could find about the character, hoping to portray a version of Wiress who was "beautiful, curious, kind of shy and uniquely capable."

"I imagine that she probably lost some allies and some friends in her games, and that emotionally attaching to these young people now would be a living nightmare," Hawke says about Wiress' relationships with the District 12 tributes. "It's like I'm trying to see them as pigs, and could one of these pigs work for my protest? I'm trying not to see them as human, and what I tried to build in was that she slowly starts to see them as human, and that's how she gets so messed up."

Mags, the winner of the 11th Hunger Games from District 4, mentors the District 12 tributes for the 50th games. She is played by Lili Taylor, who also starred in “The Conjuring,” “Mystic Pizza” and “American Crime,” and was originated by Lynn Cohen in “The Hunger Games: Catching Fire.”

Taylor tells Variety she avoided relying too heavily on Cohen's performance, instead focusing on who Mags was at this particular point in her life rather than the character's eventual fate. Working with director Francis Lawrence, the two created a version of Mags that served as a motherly figure to her tributes.

“In some ways, Mags just really cares about those young mentees and will do whatever she can to help them, even under the circumstances,” she says. “It’s so strange when you really think about it deeply, but it’s sort of like they [the tributes] have a job to do, and I really like them, and I want them to do well.”

Jennifer Lawrence reprises her role as Katniss Everdeen, the protagonist of the original “Hunger Games” films. Reaped for the 74th games, the District 12 tribute became the face of the rebellion with her mockingjay pin, which was passed down from Maysilee Donner. Since joining the franchise in 2012, Lawrence has starred in films including “Silver Linings Playbook,” “Die My Love” and “No Hard Feelings.”

Peeta Mellark is Katniss’ fellow District 12 victor of the 74th Hunger Games and her love interest in the original films, making him a key role in the rebellion. Josh Hutcherson returns to the role 11 years after the release of “The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 2″ and has since starred in the “Five Nights at Freddy’s” films and “I Love LA.”

The role of Haymitch Abernathy was originated by Woody Harrelson in the original films, where he served as the heavy-drinking, hard-shelled mentor to Katniss and Peeta. Secretly conspiring with Capitol insiders, Haymitch helped launch the start of the rebellion and oversaw the dethroning of President Snow. Harrelson's additional credits include "Cheers," "Brothers" and "Now You See Me."

Proserpina Trinket is Effie’s younger sister and a Capitol prep team member assigned to Haymitch for the Quarter Quell. Played by Iris Apatow, the university student is constantly worrying her grade will be affected due to Magno’s failure to dress the District 12 tributes. Apatow’s previous credits include “Funny People,” “Knocked Up” and “This is 40.”

Working alongside Proserpina, Vitus is also a part of Haymitch’s Capitol prep team who is similarly apprehensive about how his grade will be affected. He is played by Edvin Ryding, who previously starred in “28 Years Later” and “Mother Goose.”

Ben Wang plays Wyatt Callow, the first male tribute from District 12 to be reaped. He and his family are widely known throughout the district as the “booker boys,” a name that reflects their illegal gambling business that takes bets on the annual Hunger Games. Wang plays the character after appearing in films like “The Long Walk,” “Karate Kid: Legends” and “Mean Girls.”

Molly McCann stars as Louella, Haymitch’s young neighbor in District 12 who is also selected to fight in the Quarter Quell. Often styled in two braids and having earned the nickname “sweetheart” by Haymitch, Louella offers many similarities to Katniss.

Iona Bell plays Lou Lou, a lookalike of Louella McCoy assigned by President Snow to serve as a District 12 tribute. Though her origins in the film are unknown, she was said to be from District 11 in Collins’ novel. This is Bell's first major film role.

Ampert is a District 3 tribute who is also the son of former victor Beetee Latier. He created the Newcomers alliance that would outnumber the Careers and helped Haymitch with his plans inside the arena. Ampert is played by Percy Daggs IV, who has also acted in “Never Let Go” and “Paradise.”

Silka is one of the female Careers — a tribute who’s trained to compete in the games from a young age — from District 1. Played by Laura Marcus, Silka is set on targeting Maysilee from their early interactions during training. Marcus’ credits also include “Death by Lightning” and “The Jetty.”

Panache is one of two male tributes from District 1 and a member of the Careers who personally targeted Haymitch since their first interaction, physically attacking him during training and vowing to kill him in the arena. He’s played by Jhaleil Swaby, who also appeared in “Neagley” earlier this year.

Rada Rae plays Wellie, one of the two female tributes from District 6. Though her role in the film is relatively limited, Wellie forms a trusting friendship with Haymitch in the novel, with the protagonist vowing to protect her as much as he could in the arena. Rae previously starred in Netflix’s “Exterritorial.”

Ringina is a District 7 tribute who is a part of the Newcomers alliance. She is played by Tatyana Muzondo, who is making her film debut.

Salimou Thiam plays District 9 tribute Clayton, who joins the Newcomers alongside Haymitch and Ampert.

Smylie Bradwell stars as Haymitch’s younger brother, Sid, who is two years short of having his name entered in the annual reaping. Largely introduced to audiences via “Hamnet,” Bradwell has also starred in “Faith” and “The Crow Girl.”

Burdock is the future father of Katniss Everdeen and Haymitch’s best friend in District 12. Played by Scot Greenan, Burdock first began dating Asterid around the second Quarter Quell and is also Lenore Dove’s distant relative. Phillip Troy Linger played the character in the original films.

Asterid is the future mother of Katniss who first began dating Burdock during the events of the second Quarter Quell. She is also a close friend of the Donner twins, standing with them at the reaping and sharing an emotional goodbye after Maysilee’s name was called.
